  144. Ch 2 Internet Access and Children’s Rights: The Supreme Court held that internet access is a fundamental right, including for children, and rejected blanket bans on children's internet use.
    • Case: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish; order delivered on October 15, 2026.
    • Bench: Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran.
    • Right flows from Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a); children have it irrespective of age.
    • Blanket limits called disproportionate; Court suggested parental supervision, child modes, private-by-default accounts.
    • Limits on inherently harmful content and services remain allowed.
    • Centre must build a National Hash & URL List Database to detect and remove CSEAM.

    • PUCL v. Union of India (2003): voters' right to information about candidates upheld.

  173. Ch 2 Protection for Women in Live-in Relationships: The Supreme Court held that Section 498A IPC protection against cruelty can extend to women in live-in relationships 'in the nature of marriage'.

    • Two conditions: relationship in the nature of marriage, and a genuine intention to marry.
    • The woman bears the initial burden of proving both conditions.
    • Section 498A IPC punished cruelty by husband or his relatives: up to three years and fine.
    • Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the matching offence is Section 85.

  176. Ch 2 The Public Examinations Prevention of Unfair Means Amendment Act 2026: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026 sharply raises penalties for exam cheating and sets fast-track trials.

    • Amends the 2024 Act; covers UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS, NTA and central ministries.
    • Individuals: jail raised from 3–5 to 5–10 years; maximum fine ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh.
    • Service providers: fine up to ₹5 crore (from ₹1 crore); debarment up to eight years (from four).
    • Organised crime: 7–10 years' jail and a minimum ₹10 crore fine.
    • Investigation within two months; Special Fast Track Courts to finish trials within three months of charge sheet.

Political / National Affairs

Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan full text

  • Inaugurated on October 23, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; event ran 23–25 October.
  • Over 9,000 participants from India and abroad were expected.
  • PM interacted with a 'Holobot' (holographic image) of Swami Chinmayananda; recalled their 1993 Vadodara meeting.
  • Swami Chinmayananda (born Balakrishna Menon, 8 May 1916; died 3 August 1993) founded Chinmaya Mission in 1953.
  • His Gita Gyana Yagnas took Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads and Vedanta teachings to the public.
  • PM's focus: culture, social unity, self-reliance and youth role in Viksit Bharat by 2047.

UDAN Completes 10 Years Must knowfull text

  • RCS-UDAN = Regional Connectivity Scheme – Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik; follows National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016.
  • First UDAN flight: Shimla–Delhi, April 2017.
  • By October 2026: 687 routes and 95 aerodromes (including 17 heliports, two water aerodromes).
  • Over 3.68 lakh flights carried 1.72 crore passengers.
  • Operational airports rose from 74 (2014) to 166 (2026); India is world's third-largest domestic aviation market.
  • Modified UDAN (4 July 2026): ₹28,840 crore, FY 2026–27 to 2035–36; 100 airports, 200 helipads.

Memory aid UDAN = 'Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik' – let the common citizen of the country fly.

Don't confuse Don't confuse the launch (21 October 2016) with the first flight (Shimla–Delhi, April 2017).

Internet Access and Children’s Rights Must knowfull text

  • Case: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish; order delivered on October 15, 2026.
  • Bench: Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran.
  • Right flows from Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a); children have it irrespective of age.
  • Blanket limits called disproportionate; Court suggested parental supervision, child modes, private-by-default accounts.
  • Limits on inherently harmful content and services remain allowed.
  • Centre must build a National Hash & URL List Database to detect and remove CSEAM.

RTI Act Completes 21 Years Must knowfull text

  • Presidential assent: 15 June 2005; fully operational: 12 October 2005.
  • Right to Know comes from Article 19(1)(a) – freedom of speech and expression.
  • State of U.P. v. Raj Narain (1975): SC recognised citizens' right to know about public acts.
  • PUCL v. Union of India (2003): voters' right to information about candidates upheld.
  • The RTI Act replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.
  • It set up the Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions.

Don't confuse Don't confuse assent (15 June 2005) with full operation (12 October 2005), the date used for the anniversary.

SARAS Mela 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Held 13–31 October 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.
  • Organised under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).
  • About 1,500 SHG women and Lakhpati Didis from 34 states/UTs; more than 650 stalls.
  • Main attraction: a 16-foot installation, 'SHAKTI – The Spirit of Lakhpati Didi'.
  • First National SARAS Mela: Delhi, 1999, with about 65 beneficiaries.
  • So far 117 National SARAS Melas; annual sales exceed ₹200 crore.

Don't confuse The first-ever SARAS Mela was in Delhi (1999); Vijayawada 2026 is the first National SARAS Mela outside Delhi-NCR.

Inauguration of a Section of Chennai Metro Rail Phase II full text

  • Poonamallee–Vadapalani metro stretch cost about ₹4,900 crore.
  • It has a 3.7-km double-decker structure and signalling designed for driverless operation.
  • Highway projects (about ₹3,700 crore): 36-km Vadugapatti–Therkuvenganallur (NH-744), 30-km Madurai Ring Road (NH-744A).
  • Rail projects over ₹750 crore, including Karaikal–Peralam line; five Amrit Bharat Stations inaugurated.
  • Ports: four projects at Chennai Port, eight at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, Coal Berth-3 at Kamarajar Port.
  • Dedicated the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya–Grameen Kaushalya Yojana 2.0 Must knowfull text

  • DDU-GKY: Centrally Sponsored Scheme, launched 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission.
  • For youth aged 15–35 from poor rural households; courses last three to twelve months.
  • DDU-GKY 2.0: targets of over nine lakh candidates given to all 31 participating states/UTs for 2026–28.
  • 24 states/UTs allotted 5.6 lakh candidates across 1,200+ projects; about 2,015 batches for 70,000 youth.
  • Since 2014–15: 18.47 lakh trained for 800+ job types; 12.43 lakh got jobs.
  • Revised 2.0 guidelines: May 2025. Goa leads preparations; J&K allocated 100% targets, started 91%.

Don't confuse DDU-GKY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2014 under NRLM; 2.0 is its new round for 2026–28.

Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) Must knowfull text

  • ITLA is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV); approved by the Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi.
  • It will be the national apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research and appraisal.
  • It will prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of ten years or more.
  • It will technically appraise Government of India infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.
  • It will build a National Transport Data Repository (NTDR).
  • NTDR data: GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS systems and urban traffic systems.

Memory aid ITLA links four modes in one plan: road, rail, water and air.

100 Years of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Must knowfull text

  • Centenary event 'Manthan': Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, 30 September–1 October 2026.
  • Lee Commission (1924, Arthur Hamilton Lee) recommended it; set up under PSC (Functions) Rules, 1926.
  • First Chairman: Sir Ross Barker; office at Metcalfe House, Delhi.
  • Renamed Federal PSC (1 April 1937), then Union PSC (26 January 1950).
  • 1947: H.K. Kripalani first Indian Chairman; 1979: three-stage exam; 2011: CSAT introduced.
  • Satyendranath Tagore first Indian in ICS (joined 1864); ICS exam first held in India 1922 at Allahabad.

Memory aid 1926 → 1937 → 1950: PSC → Federal PSC → Union PSC.

Don't confuse Sir Ross Barker = first Chairman (1926); H.K. Kripalani = first Indian Chairman (1947). Tagore passed in 1863 but joined in 1864.

Panchayat Development Planning for 2027-28 Must knowfull text

  • Theme: 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'; started on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2026.
  • PPC, also called Jan Yojana Abhiyan, was first launched on 2 October 2018; held every year.
  • Over 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on GPDP and Panchayat NIRNAY portals.
  • Three levels: Gram (GPDP), Block (BPDP) and District (DPDP) Panchayat Development Plans.
  • SHG federations prepare Village Prosperity and Resilience Plans (VPRPs).
  • Over 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats upload GPDPs on eGramSwaraj; 18.13 lakh plans uploaded (2019–20 to 2025–26).

Don't confuse Campaign year 2026–27 prepares plans for financial year 2027–28.

National Coastal Mission 2.0 Must knowfull text

  • Guidelines launched on September 30, 2026 in New Delhi.
  • Central Sector Scheme of MoEFCC; outlay ₹767 crore for 2025–26 to 2030–31.
  • Earlier National Coastal Mission subsumed into NCM 2.0 from 16 May 2025.
  • NCM 1.0 (2021–22 to 2025–26) backed mangrove and coral-reef conservation and beach development.
  • Covers nine coastal States and four Union Territories.
  • Andaman & Nicobar: mangrove restoration; Gujarat: Conservation and Information Centre cum Marine Oceanarium planned.

Don't confuse NCM 2.0 took over the old mission on 16 May 2025; only its guidelines came on 30 September 2026.

Lakshadweep and Jammu & Kashmir Declared Fully Literate State Must knowfull text

  • Lakshadweep (11 Oct 2026, by Administrator Praful Patel) became fully literate; J&K was 10th since June 2024.
  • ULLAS = Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society; for people aged 15+ who missed school.
  • Fully literate = at least 95% of people aged 15 and above can read and write.
  • Firsts: Ladakh (24 June 2024) first administrative unit; Mizoram (20 May 2025) first state.
  • Sikkim fifth state (27 May 2026); Uttarakhand sixth state (8 July 2026, 98.7%).
  • Sikkim: first paperless State judiciary, declared 1 May 2026 by CJI Surya Kant in Gangtok.

Memory aid Ladakh first unit (2024), Mizoram first state (2025): L comes before M.

Don't confuse Himachal was the fifth State/UT (fourth state, September 2025); Sikkim was the fifth state (May 2026).

Five New Entries in UNESCO Tentative List Entries Must knowfull text

  • Announced on September 29, 2026; India's Tentative List now totals 78.
  • Bagh Cave Paintings: nine Buddhist caves beside the Baghni River (Madhya Pradesh).
  • Udayagiri Caves: 20 caves, mainly from late fourth and early fifth centuries, under Gupta patronage.
  • Chambal Valley Temples (Morena): Bateshwar, Padavali, Kakanmath; Nagara style; Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata patronage.
  • Ginnorgarh Fort: Raj Gond fortified capital in Sehore district.
  • Sites of Satyagraha: nine sites, seven in India and two in South Africa (incl. Phoenix Settlement).

Memory aid Pairs: Bagh – Baghni River; Ginnorgarh – Sehore; Chambal temples – Morena; Udayagiri – Gupta.

9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Venue: Rudraksh International Cooperation and Convention Centre, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.
  • Led by the Ministry of Women and Child Development; ran 9 September–8 October 2026.
  • Theme: 'Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari' (Our Anganwadi, Our Responsibility).
  • Poshan Maah = National Nutrition Month, observed every September under the POSHAN framework.
  • Five priorities include dietary diversity and protein, hot-cooked meals, and maternal nutrition with PMMVY.

Memory aid The 9th edition began on the 9th (9 September).

Cheetah Population in India Must knowfull text

  • Mother KJP21 (32 months, Indian-born) is the third Indian-born female to give birth; father from Botswana.
  • Indian-born cheetahs: 41 after the births, 40 after the Aasha cub died (12 October 2026).
  • Project Cheetah launched at Kuno on 17 September 2022 with eight Namibian cheetahs.
  • Imports: eight from Namibia, 12 from South Africa (2023), nine from Botswana (2026); total 29.
  • Programme expanded to Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (Madhya Pradesh) in 2025.
  • Project uses African cheetah (A. j. jubatus); India's native Asiatic subspecies (A. j. venaticus) is Critically Endangered.

Don't confuse Total population 60 → 59, but Indian-born 41 → 40; cumulative imports are 29.

PRAMAAN Certificates full text

  • Presented in New Delhi on September 29, 2026.
  • Scheme: Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), launched by the Ministry in December 2023.
  • Operating agency: Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal.
  • First certificates: Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (33,000 hectares of plantations) and farmer Govind Mohapatra (Odisha).
  • PRAMAAN = Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of Sustainable Management Practices for Agroforestry And Natural Forestry Resources.
  • PRAMAAN is an important tool for Indian producers, exporters and forest-based enterprises.

Memory aid PRAMAAN sounds like 'प्रमाण' (proof): a certificate that proves sustainable forestry.

GOBARdhan Fuelling Clean Energy and Rural Growth Must knowfull text

  • GOBARdhan = Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan; Cabinet approved it on 6 August 2026.
  • Central Sector Scheme led by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; ₹23,731 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2035-36.
  • Converts crop residue, cattle dung and municipal organic waste into clean energy and organic manure.
  • Original GOBARdhan began in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen).
  • Unified scheme merges CBG parts earlier run by four ministries; builds on SATAT.
  • By 6 August 2026: 1,908 registered plants, 217 commissioned, 339 under construction.

Memory aid GOBAR-dhan: cow dung (गोबर) turned into wealth (धन).

Don't confuse Cabinet approval 6 August 2026 vs formal launch 1 October 2026; the original GOBARdhan dates to 2018.

Bharat Taxi Must knowfull text

  • UP cities: Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj.
  • Operator: Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), registered under Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002.
  • STCL established 6 June 2025; national launch 5 February 2026.
  • Authorised share capital ₹300 crore, in shares of ₹100 each.
  • Drivers are called Saarthis (also Sarathis); services include cab, auto, bike and rentals.
  • Safety: driver and vehicle checks, trip records, SOS and journey-sharing.

Don't confuse Three dates: STCL set up 6 June 2025, national launch 5 February 2026, UP launch 23 September 2026.

Consumer Justice Report 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released March 2026; title 'Assessing the Capacity of Redressal Commissions in India'.
  • Five themes, 11 equally weighted indicators; score out of ten; 19 large/mid and nine small states ranked.
  • Top: Andhra Pradesh (6.28) large/mid; Meghalaya (5.58) small; Uttar Pradesh 10th (4.36).
  • Pending cases rose about 21%: 4.27 lakh (end 2019) to 5.15 lakh (end 2024).
  • About 35% of cases pending over three years; Kerala about 79%, Uttar Pradesh about 62%.
  • CVC's 62nd Annual Report (2025): CVOs got 70,584 complaints directly; 64,905 disposed.

Don't confuse IJR's report ranks consumer commissions; the CVC report (also in this news) is about vigilance complaints.

First Census of Springs 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released at the valedictory of the ninth India International Water Week, Bharat Mandapam; chaired by C. R. Patil.
  • Manipur has the most springs (3,941), followed by Maharashtra (3,652).
  • Reference year 2023–24; figures cover only these ten states, not all of India.
  • States: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Maharashtra, Manipur, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Tripura, West Bengal.
  • Rajasthan recorded the fewest (13); Andhra Pradesh's 34 springs are all seasonal.
  • Earlier Volume II (Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu) came out on 23 March 2026.

Don't confuse 14,468 is a ten-state total, not an all-India spring count.

Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme Must knowfull text

  • Electronics exports rose from over ₹38,000 crore (FY 2014–15) to ₹4.24 lakh crore (FY 2025–26).
  • As of August 2026: manufacturing started at 38 plants; 16 projects at advanced stages.
  • ECMS notified on 8 April 2025; outlay raised from ₹22,919 crore to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.
  • Turnover-linked incentives for six years (plus optional one-year gestation); capex incentives for five years.
  • Electronics production rose from ₹1.9 lakh crore (FY 2014–15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (FY 2025–26).
  • National target by 2030: $500 billion electronics manufacturing and $150 billion exports.

Don't confuse India's 2030 targets ($500 billion ecosystem, $150 billion exports) are separate from ECMS project outcomes.

Special Constitutional Safeguards for Ladakh Must knowfull text

  • Proposed at a 9 September 2026 meeting with Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).
  • Body would make laws on land, culture, language, forests, environment and natural resources.
  • 'Sui generis' model = unique arrangement; no automatic statehood or regular UT legislature.
  • Ladakh became a UT without a legislature on October 31, 2019 (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019).
  • Local demands: statehood, Sixth Schedule, job safeguards, separate Lok Sabha seats for Leh and Kargil.
  • Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2), 275(1)) covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.

Memory aid Sixth Schedule states = 'AMTM': Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.

Don't confuse Article 371-K is only a proposal; it is not statehood and not Sixth Schedule status.

Twin Flower Fields in Leh full text

  • Opened on Sewa Diwas to mark PM Narendra Modi's 76th birthday.
  • Located at Choglamsar and Stakna; altitude 10,600 feet; 40 acres together.
  • Over 25 lakh flowers: about 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus.
  • Foundation stone laid on June 22, 2026; MoU with CSIR–IHBT, Palampur (Himachal Pradesh).
  • Agriculture Department develops the fields, then hands them to SHGs and cooperatives at bloom.
  • First air consignment (29 September 2026): 15,000 A-grade Lilium stems from KBR Airport, Leh, for Delhi, Mumbai, Chandigarh.

Kavach 4.0 Must knowfull text

  • Varanasi division: announced September 28, 2026; ₹223 crore; 614.75 route km.
  • Izzatnagar division: announced August 12, 2026; ₹295 crore (estimated); 660 route km.
  • Kavach was developed by RDSO (Research Designs and Standards Organisation) with Indian industry.
  • Functions: enforce permitted speed, prevent Signal Passing at Danger (SPAD), reduce collision risk.
  • RDSO approved the Kavach 4.0 specification on 16 July 2024.
  • 4.0 upgrades: better location accuracy, signal data in big yards, OFC station link, electronic interlocking interface.

Don't confuse Varanasi: ₹223 crore, 614.75 km; Izzatnagar: ₹295 crore, 660 km – don't swap.

Assam Uniform Civil Code Act, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Bill introduced 25 May 2026 by Atul Bora; passed by voice vote on 27 May 2026.
  • Assam is the third state, after Uttarakhand and Gujarat, to adopt a state UCC law.

  • Period: FY 2026–27 to 2035–36; funded by Government of India budget support.
  • Plans 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips; ₹12,159 crore over eight years.
  • O&M support for three years: up to ₹3.06 crore per airport and ₹0.90 crore per heliport/water aerodrome yearly.
  • About ₹2,577 crore proposed for around 441 aerodromes.
  • UDAN launched October 2016 to make flying affordable and link Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
  • By June 2026: 665 routes, 95 airports/heliports/water aerodromes; 1.64 crore passengers on 3.5 lakh+ flights.

Don't confuse Title says 'Modified UDAN', text says 'Revised UDAN' – same scheme, ₹28,840 crore, approved 25 March 2026.

Republic Day 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Chief Guests: Antonio Costa (European Council President) and Ursula von der Leyen (European Commission President).
  • 30 tableaux: 17 from States/UTs and 13 from Union Ministries.
  • Sub-themes: 'Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram' and 'Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat'.
  • Best State tableaux (judges): Maharashtra (Ganeshotsav) first, then Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala.
  • Best Ministry tableau: Ministry of Culture; Special Prize: Central Public Works Department.
  • Popular Choice (MyGov poll): Gujarat first, Uttar Pradesh (Culture of Bundelkhand) second, Rajasthan third.

Don't confuse Judges' best tableau = Maharashtra; Popular Choice best = Gujarat (UP second).

Supreme Court stays 2026 UGC Equity Regulations Must knowfull text

  • Court flagged vagueness, possible misuse and exclusion in the 2026 Regulations.
  • The Regulations followed SC directions in Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India (2019).
  • A Bench of Justices Surya Kant and Ujjal Bhuyan had directed UGC to notify enforceable rules.
  • Caste discrimination defined to cover SCs, STs and OBCs.
  • Every institution must set up an Equal Opportunity Centre with an Equity Committee headed by the institution head.
  • Equity Committee meets within 24 hours, reports in 15 working days; head acts within 7 days.

Memory aid 24 hours – 15 working days – 7 days: meet, report, act.

Water Budgeting in Aspirational Blocks full text

  • Covers 18 Aspirational Blocks in 10 States and a UT, using a digital water-budgeting platform.
  • Severe deficits: Namchi (94%), Gangiri (60%), Baldeogarh (53%).
  • Kotri and Abu Road (Rajasthan) over-extract groundwater beyond recharge.
  • Fatehpur (Bihar) generates runoff but fails to use the stored water well.
  • Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Bihar Legislative Assembly Election Results, 2025 full text

  • Polling in two phases: 6 and 11 November 2025 (121 and 122 seats); counting 14 November.
  • Turnout 67.25%, the highest since 1951; women 71.77%, men 62.73%.
  • BJP largest party with 89 seats; JD(U) 85; Mahagathbandhan reduced to 35.
  • RJD won 25 seats but had the highest vote share (23%).
  • Nitish Kumar sworn in on 20 November 2025 (10th time); resigned on 14 April 2026.
  • Samrat Chaudhary became Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister on 15 April 2026.

Don't confuse Largest party by seats = BJP (89); highest vote share = RJD (23%).

Kashi Tamil Sangamam 4.0 Must knowfull text

  • Theme: 'Let Us Learn Tamil – Tamil Karkalam'.
  • Valedictory ceremony on 30 December 2025 with Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan.
  • Anchored by the Ministry of Education; IIT Madras and BHU are principal knowledge partners.
  • Aligned with Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat; Government of Uttar Pradesh also takes part.
  • KTS 1.0: 2022; KTS 2.0: Dec 2023 at Namo Ghat; KTS 3.0: Feb 2025 on Sage Agastya.

Memory aid Tamil Karkalam = 'Let us learn Tamil'.

Union Cabinet Approves 2027 Census Must knowfull text

  • Eighth Census since Independence; the last completed Census was in 2011.
  • Census is a Union subject: Entry 69, Union List, Seventh Schedule; Census Act, 1948.
  • Phase I Houselisting: 1 April–30 September 2026; Phase II Population Enumeration: February 2027.
  • Reference date: 00:00 hours, 1 March 2027 (Ladakh and snow-bound areas enumerated September 2026).
  • Caste enumeration included (CCPA decision, April 30, 2025); 40-question schedule, Question 10 on caste.
  • Registrar General (under MHA) runs it; Android/iOS apps; about 30 lakh field staff; optional online self-enumeration.

Memory aid 16th Census, 8th after Independence; the count 'freezes' at midnight, 1 March 2027.

Don't confuse Approval date (12 December 2025) is not the reference date (00:00 hours, 1 March 2027). Census 2021 was postponed after COVID-19.

News in Short Must knowfull text

  • 12th International Yoga Day (21 June 2026): Kolkata, Red Road; theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'; Guinness record.
  • Cabinet approved renaming 'Kerala' as 'Keralam' on 24 February 2026 (Assembly resolution: 24 June 2024).
  • PM-RAHAT (launched 13 February 2026): treatment cover up to ₹1.5 lakh per accident victim for 7 days.
  • UP Rural Abadi Records (Gharauni) Act: Governor's assent 2 January 2026; gives legal basis to SVAMITVA property cards.
  • BHASHINI (BHASHa INterface for India): 36+ text languages, 22+ voice languages, 350+ AI models.
  • Ayodhya, 25 November 2025: PM hoisted Dharma Dhwaja (10 ft × 20 ft) on Ram Temple Shikhara.

Don't confuse PM-RAHAT was launched on 13 February 2026 but got its official name by notification on 19 February 2026.

International Affairs (अंतरराष्ट्रीय परिदृश्य)

77 topics · 59 marked Must know · 100 practice questions

India and It’s Neighbours; Other Asian Countries

India–Switzerland Must knowfull text

  • Visit October 5–7, 2026; talks at Hyderabad House; focus on 3Ts — Trade, Technology, Talent.
  • EFTA (set up 1960): Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland; Switzerland is not in the EEA.
  • TEPA: signed 10 March 2024, entered into force 1 October 2025.
  • TEPA goal: US$100 billion investment and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years.
  • Young Professionals pact: 300 professionals a year from each country, expandable to 500.
  • Second India–EFTA Prosperity Summit: Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, 7 October 2026.

Memory aid EFTA's four = 'I Like Nice Sweets': Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland.

Don't confuse TEPA was signed on 10 March 2024 but came into force on 1 October 2025; don't swap the two dates.

India-Japan Must knowfull text

  • Abe Memorial Corridor (Rudraksh Centre, Varanasi) opened 7 October 2026 by CM Yogi Adityanath and Akie Abe.
  • Rudraksh Centre (Japanese-aided) opened by Modi on 15 July 2021; Abe received Padma Vibhushan in 2021.
  • UP: 500-acre Japan City planned in YEIDA region; Yamanashi Prefecture partners UP on green hydrogen.
  • 16th Annual Summit: Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi in New Delhi, 1–3 July 2026; 16 official outcomes.
  • UNICORN = Unified Complex Radio Antenna, a naval defence co-development, announced outside the 16 outcomes.
  • ISRO–JAXA LUPEX = Chandrayaan-5; 2027 = Year of Shared Horizons (75 years of diplomatic ties).

Memory aid 16th Summit → 16 official outcomes: the summit number equals the outcome count.

Don't confuse UNICORN was announced separately; it is NOT one of the 16 official outcomes.

PM Modi’s State Visit to Uzbekistan Must knowfull text

  • Visit: 29–30 August 2026, on the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
  • Strategic Partnership (2011) upgraded to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
  • Modi received the 'Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik' Order, Uzbekistan's highest state award.
  • Uzbekistan (double-landlocked): about 7,000 tonnes uranium output in 2025; reserves 139,000 tonnes.
  • Trade target US$5 billion by 2030; NIPL–NIPC deal lets UPI apps scan UZQR codes.
  • Exercise DUSTLIK (7th edition) held in Namangan Region, April 2026; LoI to conserve Fayaz Tepa, Kara Tepa.

Don't confuse Two trade figures: US$5 billion target by 2030 (summit) vs Goyal's call to double ~US$1.5 billion to ~US$3 billion in three years.

India–Seychelles Must knowfull text

  • Visit: 27–29 June 2026; talks with President Dr Patrick Herminie.
  • Modi's second visit, after March 2015; advanced the SESEL Joint Vision of February 2026.
  • 19 outcomes: five development-assistance measures, five announcements, nine agreements/MoUs.
  • India gifted Fast Patrol Vessel PS Lespwar to the Seychelles Coast Guard.
  • Seychelles decided to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.
  • NPCI International and Central Bank of Seychelles signed an MoU to implement UPI.

Memory aid 19 outcomes = 5 + 5 + 9 (assistance + announcements + agreements).

India–Cyprus Strategic Partnership full text

  • First India visit of President Christodoulides in his current role; Business Forum held in Mumbai.
  • Diplomatic ties since February 17, 1962; 65th anniversary to be marked in 2027.
  • Five-year defence cooperation roadmap for 2026–2031 welcomed.
  • MoU between NPCI International Payments Limited and Eurobank Cyprus.
  • UPI to be made interoperable with the ECB's TIPS (Target Instant Payment Settlement) system.

Memory aid 1962 + 65 = 2027: the 65th anniversary year.

Myanmar President’s Visit to India Must knowfull text

  • Visit: May 30 to June 3, 2026; his first foreign trip since taking office.
  • Prayed at Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya, and visited Sujata Temple.
  • Toured NTPC's research arm NETRA complex in Greater Noida (clean energy research).
  • Kaladan route: Sittwe Port → Paletwa (inland waterway) → Zorinpui, Mizoram (road).
  • Both sides pushed to finish the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway.
  • Mekong Ganga ICCR scholarships for Myanmar students raised from 36 to 100.

Memory aid Kaladan = S-P-Z: Sittwe (port) → Paletwa (river) → Zorinpui (road, Mizoram).

India – UAE Must knowfull text

  • May 15, 2026: Modi in Abu Dhabi; tour order UAE, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, Italy.
  • ISPRL–ADNOC MoU: up to 30 million barrels of ADNOC crude in India's strategic reserves.
  • Reserve sites: Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Chandikhol (Odisha); Fujairah framework in the UAE.
  • Cochin Shipyard–Drydocks World MoU: Ship Repair Cluster at Vadinar; C-DAC–G42: 8-exaflop supercomputer.
  • MAITRI (Master Application for International Trade and Regulatory Interface) runs the Virtual Trade Corridor.
  • January 19, 2026 visit of UAE President: HPCL–ADNOC Gas 10-year deal, 0.5 million tonnes LNG yearly from 2028.

Don't confuse ISPRL–ADNOC = crude oil storage; IOCL–ADNOC = LPG supplies; HPCL–ADNOC Gas = LNG.

India – North America

India–Canada Relations Must knowfull text

  • Visit: February 27 to March 2, 2026; 79 years of India–Canada diplomatic ties in 2026.
  • Cameco–Department of Atomic Energy deal: about CAD 2.6 billion, long-term uranium supply.
  • India's Viksit Bharat vision linked with Canada's 'Build Canada Strong' agenda.
  • Canada–India Pulse Protein Centre of Excellence proposed at NIFTEM Kundli.
  • AICTE–Mitacs MoU: about 300 Indian undergraduates yearly for Canadian research internships, from 2027.
  • Trade goal: about CAD 70 billion (INR 4.65 lakh crore) by 2030.

India – South America

India-Brazil full text

  • Visit: February 18-22, 2026; talks with PM Modi at Hyderabad House on 21 February.
  • Attended the India AI Impact Summit 2026 (19–20 February).
  • Lula's fifth India visit as President, sixth overall, and his second State Visit.
  • Strategic Partnership since 2006; trade target over USD 30 billion by 2030.
  • MoU: India's Ministry of Steel with Brazil's Ministry of Mines and Energy on minerals for steel.
  • Partners in BRICS, G20, IBSA, G-4, WTO and the United Nations.

Don't confuse Three counts for Lula: fifth visit as President, sixth visit overall, second State Visit.

India – Europe

State Visits of President Droupadi Murmu to Europe Must knowfull text

  • Dates: July 19–25, 2026; first Indian President to visit Moldova and North Macedonia.
  • Romania: first Indian presidential visit since Shankar Dayal Sharma in May 1994.
  • Moldova: met President Maia Sandu; KEC International built the 400-kV Vulcănesti–Chisinău line.
  • North Macedonia: met President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova; Gandhi bust unveiled in Skopje.
  • Mother Teresa was born in Skopje and received the Bharat Ratna in 1980.
  • Romania: Doctor Honoris Causa from Bucharest University of Economic Studies; 2028 = India–Romania Year of Innovation.

Don't confuse 'First-ever visit' applies only to Moldova and North Macedonia; Romania had a 1994 presidential visit.

India-UK CETA and DCC Must knowfull text

  • Operational: July 15, 2026; CETA concluded 6 May 2025, signed in London 24 July 2025.
  • DCC signed 10 February 2026; ends double social-security payments for posted workers.
  • Took 14 negotiation rounds; built on Enhanced Trade Partnership and Roadmap 2030 (May 2021).
  • CETA has 30 chapters; UK gives zero duty on nearly 99% of Indian tariff lines.
  • UK service commitments: 12 sectors and 137 sub-sectors.
  • India kept dairy, cereals, millets, apples, edible oils and oilseeds out of major concessions.

Don't confuse CETA = trade agreement; DCC = social-security convention. DCC does not automatically give host-country pensions.

India–Norway Must knowfull text

  • Visit: 18–19 May 2026; hosted by PM Jonas Gahr Støre; audience with King Harald V.
  • India–Norway relations established in February 1947.
  • Ties upgraded to a Green Strategic Partnership for climate action and green industries.
  • 3rd India–Nordic Summit, Oslo, May 19, 2026: Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership.
  • India's Arctic station Himadri is at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard; Norway joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
  • First Maritime Security, Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Dialogue: Oslo, September 11, 2025.

Don't confuse Bilateral (Norway) = Green Strategic Partnership; India–Nordic = Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership.

PM Modi’s Italy Visit Must knowfull text

  • Met PM Giorgia Meloni and President Sergio Mattarella in Rome, May 19-20, 2026.
  • Ties upgraded to a Special Strategic Partnership; annual leaders' meetings agreed.
  • Joint Strategic Action Plan 2025–2029 was adopted at the 2024 G20 Summit.
  • Trade target: €20 billion by 2029.
  • 2027 designated Year of Culture and Tourism; INNOVIT India innovation hub launched.
  • FAO headquarters, Rome: Modi received the Agricola Medal, FAO's highest honour, for food security work.

Don't confuse The Agricola Medal is given by FAO (a UN body in Rome), not by the Italian government.

India-France Must knowfull text

  • Visit: 17–19 February 2026; partnership placed under the Horizon 2047 Roadmap.
  • India-France Year of Innovation 2026 launched in Mumbai (AI, science, health, education).
  • Tata-Airbus H125 Final Assembly Line, Vamagal, Karnataka: India's first private-sector helicopter line (17 February 2026).
  • BEL–Safran joint-venture MoU to make HAMMER missiles in India.
  • France backs India's target of 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047; Jaitapur project progressed.

Memory aid 2047 twice: Horizon 2047 Roadmap and 100 GW nuclear by 2047.

Don't confuse France = 'Special Global Strategic Partnership'; Italy = 'Special Strategic Partnership' (both 2026).

India-Germany Must knowfull text

  • Visit: January 12–13, 2026; talks held in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
  • Bilateral goods and services trade crossed US$50 billion in 2024.
  • Germany: visa-free airport transit for Indian passport holders from June 3, 2026.
  • Joint Declaration of Intent on Global Skills Partnership: ethical recruitment, especially of health workers.
  • Renewable-energy skilling Centre of Excellence proposed at National Skill Training Institute, Hyderabad.

India – Africa

India–Liberia Must knowfull text

  • GoF on S4 = Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers.
  • Launched 25 September 2026 at UN HQ during the 81st UNGA; about 25 countries attended.
  • Co-chairs: Dr. S. Jaishankar and Liberian Foreign Minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti.
  • Liberia has the world's largest ship registry by Gross Tonnage; India is a major seafarer supplier.
  • Three priorities: shipping safety, maritime security, seafarers' welfare; supports IMO and ILO.
  • Key laws: UNCLOS Article 94, SOLAS Convention 1974, Maritime Labour Convention 2006.

Memory aid S4 = four S-words: Safety, Security, Shipping, Seafarers.

India–Mali full text

  • Held June 19–20, 2026, in Bamako; theme 'Reinforcing Trade and Strategic Partnerships.'
  • Chaired by Malian PM Major General Abdoulaye Maïga; India's team led by Joint Secretary Amit Kumar.
  • Bilateral trade: US$326.61 million in FY 2025–26, up 55%.
  • India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme supported trade.
  • Mali exports cotton, leather, cashew, gum arabic; India supplies pharmaceuticals, textiles, vehicles.

India-Ethiopia Must knowfull text

  • Visit: 16–17 December 2025, Addis Ababa; talks with PM Dr. Abiy Ahmed Ali.
  • Modi addressed a Joint Session of the Ethiopian Parliament.
  • Awarded the 'Great Honour Nishan of Ethiopia', the country's highest award.
  • Ties raised to a Strategic Partnership; formal diplomatic relations since 1950.
  • Second Joint Defence Cooperation meeting: Addis Ababa, September 28, 2026.
  • Addis Ababa hosts the headquarters of the African Union.

India – Oceania

PM Modi’s Australia Visit 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Visit: July 8–10, 2026; summit in Melbourne on 9 July with PM Anthony Albanese.
  • Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates from 2020; new declaration expands the 2009 security framework.
  • Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap; Indian Coast Guard–Maritime Border Command MoU.
  • Australia backed India's Nuclear Suppliers Group membership and Gaganyaan; uranium exports under IAEA safeguards.
  • Temporary tracking terminal commissioned on the Cocos Islands.
  • Sports Roadmap launched at Melbourne Cricket Ground, 10 July 2026; links 2030 CWG Ahmedabad, 2032 Brisbane Olympics.

India-New Zealand Must knowfull text

  • Visit: July 10–11, 2026, Auckland; Strategic Partnership and Roadmap to 2030 adopted.
  • First Indian prime-ministerial visit to New Zealand in four decades; ten agreements concluded.
  • FTA talks began during PM Christopher Luxon's India visit, March 2025.
  • Trade: about NZ$3.95 billion now, target NZ$7 billion by 2030.
  • NZ to facilitate US$20 billion investment over 15 years; up to 5,000 skilled visa pathways.
  • Kiwifruit Centres of Excellence planned in Nagaland and Uttarakhand.

Don't confuse The Roadmap to 2030 is not legally binding: no enforceable obligations or automatic funding.

B. International Events/Indices/Rankings/Reports

WJP Rule of Law Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released by World Justice Project on October 21, 2026; India 88th of 143, score 0.48.
  • India was 86th in 2025 (score 0.49); slipped two places.
  • Rule of law declined in 62% of countries — ninth straight year decline beat improvement.
  • Index uses eight factors, 44 sub-factors; score 0 (weakest) to 1 (strongest).
  • India: 3rd of six in South Asia; best in Open Government (45th), worst in Civil Justice (116th).
  • Top: Denmark (0.90), Norway, Finland; last: Venezuela (143rd).

Don't confuse India's 2026 score 0.48 and rank 88th vs 2025 score 0.49 and rank 86th.

Nobel Prizes 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Medicine: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel — optogenetics (light-controlled neurons); announced 5 October.
  • Physics: Francis Halzen — IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctic ice; high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.
  • Chemistry: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai — chirality (molecular handedness): asymmetric catalysis and autocatalysis.
  • Literature (8 October): Anne Carson, Canadian poet and classicist; works include Autobiography of Red, Nox.
  • Peace: Navi Pillay, South African jurist of Indian Tamil origin; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights 2008–2014.
  • Economics: Robert E. Hall (Stanford) and Michael Woodford (Columbia) — macroeconomic stabilisation (12 October).

Memory aid Optogenetics = 'opto' (light) + genetics: selected neurons switched on or off using light.

Don't confuse Two Stanford names: Karl Deisseroth (Medicine) and Robert E. Hall (Economics) are both from Stanford University.

Global Hunger Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released October 2026; 21st edition; first published in 2006.
  • Publishers: Concern Worldwide, Welthungerhilfe and IFHV.
  • India: 100th of 122, score 24.1 ('serious'); South Asia average 23.5, world 18.1.
  • Four indicators: undernourishment (1/3), child stunting (1/6), child wasting (1/6), under-five mortality (1/3).
  • India: child wasting 19.0% (main concern); stunting fell from 50% (2000) to 29.3%.
  • Last: Somalia (122nd, 47.0, 'alarming'); 24 countries share ranks 1–24.

Memory aid Weights add up to 1: undernourishment and child mortality 1/3 each; stunting and wasting 1/6 each.

Don't confuse GHI score runs backwards: 0 is best, 100 is worst — a higher score means more hunger.

WHO–UNICEF JMP Report 2026 full text

  • Released September 22, 2026: 'Progress on Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Schools 2015–2025'.
  • Tracks SDG Indicator 4.a.1; universal coverage means over 99%.
  • Global 2025: schools with basic water 78%, sanitation 77%, hygiene 72%.
  • India basic coverage: water 96.6%, sanitation 80.8% (2025); hygiene 52.9% (2024).
  • About 50 million Indian children lacked school sanitation — nearly one-fifth of the global 244 million.
  • India among 28 of 62 countries on track for universal basic drinking water.

Don't confuse Needed speed-up: fourfold for water, fivefold for sanitation; for hygiene WHO says fourfold, parts of the JMP report say fivefold.

Academic Freedom Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • 12th edition of Free to Think, by Scholars at Risk (SAR), released September 15, 2026.
  • India's Academic Freedom Index score: 0.16 (2024) → 0.14; category 'severely restricted'.
  • Report counted 382 attacks from 321 incidents in 59 countries (1 July 2025–30 June 2026).
  • AFI covers 179 countries; run by FAU (Germany) and V-Dem Institute with 2,357 experts.
  • Five indicators include freedom to research and teach, institutional autonomy and campus integrity.
  • Same category as India: Hong Kong, Indonesia, Pakistan, West Bank, Ukraine.

Don't confuse Free to Think is SAR's report; the Academic Freedom Index itself is run by FAU and the V-Dem Institute.

Global Gender Gap Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • India: 131st of 145, same rank as 2025; score up from 64.4% to 64.5%.
  • India's weakest: Political Empowerment 24.5% (67th) and Economic Participation 41.2%.
  • India's strongest: Educational Attainment 96.6%, Health and Survival 95.6%.
  • Index launched by WEF in 2006; scores 0 (disparity) to 1 (full parity).
  • Iceland first (93.0%) for the 17th straight year; Chad last (145th).
  • Globally 69.2% of the gap closed; full parity needs another 120 years.

Memory aid India's four pillars fall from school to parliament: Study 96.6, Health 95.6, Money 41.2, Power 24.5 (% parity).

Don't confuse Rank 131st is unchanged from 2025; only the score moved (64.4% → 64.5%).

India Joins Global Initiative for 6G Leadership and Security Must knowfull text

  • Followed the G20 Innovation Ministers' Meeting, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, September 1–2, 2026.
  • Initiative launched July 2026 under the US Commerce Department's NTIA.
  • India's participation coordinated by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT).
  • India aims for about 10% of global 6G standards and patents by 2030.
  • Bharat 6G Vision launched March 2023; Bharat 6G Alliance grew from 14 to 85 members.
  • India represented by MoS Jitin Prasada; around 4,000 patents contributed by March 2026.

Oxford Economics Global Cities Index 2026 full text

  • Delhi 268th (India's best), Bengaluru 311th, Mumbai 330th; no Indian city in global top 100.
  • Global top three: New York, London, Paris.
  • Index introduced in 2024 by Oxford Economics; covers 1,000 cities.
  • Five pillars: Economics, Human Capital, Quality of Life, Environment, Governance.
  • Delhi scored 57.6/100; best pillar Human Capital (13th globally).
  • Other Indian top-10: Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Thrissur, Kochi, Kolkata, Kozhikode (499th).

US–Denmark–Greenland Arctic Defense Agreement 2026 full text

  • Signed by Donald Trump, Danish PM Mette Frederiksen and Greenland PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
  • Amends the 1951 Defense Agreement (signed 27 April 1951) under the North Atlantic Treaty.
  • Earlier supplements: 1991 MoU and 2004 Igaliku Agreement.
  • Expands US activity at Pituffik Space Base (formerly Thule Air Base), north-western Greenland.
  • Recognises Denmark's sovereignty and Greenland's self-determination; refers to US Golden Dome missile defence.
  • Generally bars non-NATO countries from military bases in Greenland without the parties' agreement.

Don't confuse Pituffik Space Base and Thule Air Base are the same place (old and new names).

26th SCO Summit 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Venue: Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic; chaired by President Sadyr Japarov; 28 documents approved.
  • India's approach: Security, Connectivity and Opportunity; backed English as an SCO official language.
  • India to host the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum later in 2026.
  • SCO set up June 15, 2001 (from Shanghai Five, 1996); 10 members; Secretariat in Beijing.
  • Joined: India and Pakistan 2017, Iran 2023, Belarus 2024; RATS is in Tashkent.
  • Pakistan holds 2026–27 presidency; Lahore named SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital 2026–27.

Memory aid India's SCO approach spells S-C-O: Security, Connectivity, Opportunity.

Don't confuse Heads of State summit = 26th, Bishkek (Modi); Heads of Government meeting = 25th, Dushanbe (Rajnath Singh).

Global Passport Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Index by Global Citizen Solutions, a private advisory firm; 14 indicators.
  • Weights: Enhanced Mobility 50%, Investment 25%, Quality of Living 25%.
  • India's score 45.1; Mobility 135th, Investment 94th, Quality of Living 118th.
  • Indian passport: free access 6, visa-on-arrival 10, e-visa 64, conventional visa 88 destinations.
  • Top: Sweden (96.05); last: Afghanistan (23.10).
  • India was 127th during 2021–2023.

Memory aid Weights 50–25–25: Mobility counts double, so it moves India's rank the most.

FAO Food Price Index full text

  • FFPI: 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.7 points (0.6%) from June.
  • Still 29.1 points (18.2%) below the March 2022 peak.
  • Tracks five groups: cereals, vegetable oils, meat, dairy, sugar; base period 2014–2016.
  • Cereals up 3.4% (wheat 5.8%); sugar up 5.6%; vegetable oils up 2.0%.
  • Meat fell 2.8% from its June record; dairy fell 0.7%.
  • Higher world food prices can push domestic inflation and complicate RBI policy.

Don't confuse FFPI tracks international commodity prices, not domestic retail food prices.

World Investment Report 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released July 7, 2026 by UNCTAD (UN Trade and Development); title 'International Investment in a Turbulent Era'.
  • Global FDI up 6% to about US$1.6 trillion in 2025, ending two years of decline.
  • India inward FDI: US$27.1 billion (2024) → US$38.9 billion (2025); rank 13th → 11th.
  • India outward FDI: US$24.3 billion → US$35.7 billion; rank 20th → 18th.
  • Top FDI destination 2025: United States ($277 billion), then Singapore.
  • FDI usually means at least 10% voting power (lasting interest).

Don't confuse Inward FDI rank = 11th; outward FDI rank = 18th — don't swap.

US–Saudi Arabia Civil Nuclear Cooperation Agreement 2026 full text

  • Signed by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright (20 July, Washington) and Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman (22 July, Riyadh).
  • Legal basis: Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act, 1954.
  • Duration: 30 years after entry into force (Article 16).
  • Article 7: two-year joint study on enrichment; later enrichment needs written consent.
  • Unlike the 2009 US–UAE deal, Saudi Arabia has not renounced enrichment and reprocessing.
  • IAEA Additional Protocol not mandatory; Trump sent it to Congress on 24 August 2026.

Don't confuse 'Gold Standard' = giving up enrichment and reprocessing. The 2009 US–UAE deal has it; the Saudi deal does not.

US and Iranian Initial Peace Agreement Must knowfull text

  • June 17, 2026: Trump and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian signed the 14-point MoU electronically; mainly a ceasefire.
  • Ends fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon; Strait of Hormuz reopens toll-free within 30 days.
  • Sanctions relief: US Treasury waivers let Iran export crude oil and petroleum products.
  • Nuclear: Iran halts enrichment and down-blends (dilutes) highly enriched uranium to 3.67% under IAEA monitoring.
  • Reconstruction fund of at least $300 billion, to be financed by Gulf Arab nations; US not directly.
  • US to unfreeze Iranian assets (Tehran seeks about $24 billion); 60-day talks for a final nuclear pact.

Memory aid Hormuz in 30 days, final nuclear deal in 60 days: the harder job gets double the time.

Don't confuse $300 billion is the reconstruction fund (Gulf Arab money, not US); $24 billion is Iran's frozen assets.

Nepal’s Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 Must knowfull text

  • August 26, 2026: flash flood in Rasuwa, near the Nepal–China border, on Lhende Khola–Bhote Koshi–Trishuli rivers.

  • GLOF = flood when a glacial lake's ice or moraine dam fails.
  • The debris-laden flood damaged settlements, roads, bridges, hydropower projects and communication networks.

Don't confuse Rasuwa flood was mainly an avalanche-induced cascading hazard, not a conventional GLOF.

  • Index of Economic Freedom 2026 (Heritage Foundation): India 132nd; Global Fire Power 2026: India 4th.
  • Sustainable Development Report 2026: India 94th of 169; Democracy Index 2025 (EIU): India 47th.
  • Nature Conservation Index 2025: India 172nd of 180; International IP Index 2026: 43rd of 55.

Don't confuse Don't mix the Global Peace Index (India 127th) with the Global Terrorism Index (India 13th).

Economic Affairs (आर्थिक परिदृश्य)

A. Fiscal & Monetary Affairs

Strategic Restructuring of IDBI Bank Must knowfull text

  • Buyer: 10955230 Canada Inc.; parent company Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited.
  • Stake sold: Government of India 30.48% + LIC 30.24% = 60.72%.
  • Bid ₹81 per share vs benchmark ₹75.99 (average of two independent valuations).
  • After the sale: Government about 15%, LIC about 19%.
  • Started as Industrial Development Bank of India on 1 July 1964; banking company from 1 October 2004.
  • RBI classed it a private sector bank from 21 January 2019, after LIC bought 51%.

Memory aid 60.72 = 30.48 (Govt) + 30.24 (LIC): two near-30s add up to about 61.

Don't confuse CCEA (Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs) approved the buyer; the deal is still subject to regulatory conditions.

57th GST Council Meeting Must knowfull text

  • 57th GST Council meeting: New Delhi, October 8, 2026; chair Nirmala Sitharaman.
  • Simpler registration form FORM GST REG-01; auto-approval of amendments except Principal Place of Business (PPoB).
  • Rule 14B: simple registration route for small e-commerce sellers.
  • Refund acknowledgement/deficiency memo time cut from 15 days to 10 days.
  • Minimum tax amount for issuing a show-cause notice: ₹10,000.
  • ITC on input services received on or after 1 November 2026 to count for inverted duty refunds.

Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy (October, 2026) Must knowfull text

  • Repo rate up 25 basis points: 5.25% to 5.50%; decision unanimous.
  • From 7 October 2026: SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%.
  • RBI forecast for FY 2026–27: real GDP growth 7.1%, CPI inflation 5.2%, core inflation 4.4%.
  • Actual Q1 FY 2026–27 (April–June 2026) real GDP growth: 7.8% (MoSPI).
  • Inflation target 4% (band 2% to 6%) for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
  • September CPI (released 12 October 2026, provisional): headline 5.54%, food 7.74%; base 2024=100.

Don't confuse 7.1% is RBI's full-year FY 2026–27 forecast; 7.8% is the actual Q1 growth. 5.2% is projected CPI; 5.54% is September's actual.

Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Amends Section 13 of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
  • Presidential assent: August 6, 2026; in force: October 1, 2026.
  • Delay over one year but within two years: order of DM, SDM or authorised Executive Magistrate (Section 13(3)).
  • Delay over two years: order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class (Section 13(3A)).
  • Normal reporting time: 21 days; registration within 30 days needs a late fee.
  • Start date notified by Registrar General, India (MHA) through S.O. 5081(E), 16 September 2026.

Don't confuse Under the 2023 amendment every delay over one year needed a DM/SDM order; the 2026 Act shifts over-two-year cases to a Judicial Magistrate.

PMJDY Completes 12 Years Must knowfull text

  • Launched by PM Narendra Modi on 28 August 2014.
  • Accounts: 14.72 crore (2015) to 59.09 crore (19 August 2026), about fourfold.
  • Women hold 32.92 crore accounts (about 55.7%); rural and semi-urban 45.95 crore (77.8%).
  • Deposits: ₹15,670 crore (March 2015) to ₹3,16,514 crore (August 2026); average ₹5,356 per account.
  • Accident cover ₹2 lakh for accounts opened after August 28, 2018; overdraft up to ₹10,000.
  • Guinness record (January 2015): 18,096,130 accounts opened in one week, August 23-29, 2014.

Memory aid Same birthday: launched 28 August 2014, 12 years on 28 August 2026.

CBDC-Based Food Subsidy Distribution under PMGKAY Must knowfull text

  • CBDC-based DBT for PMGKAY launched in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli on August 14, 2026.
  • Launched by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
  • Pilots: Gujarat by Amit Shah (February 15, 2026); Puducherry by Prahlad Joshi (February 26, 2026).
  • Digital Rupee (e₹) is a tokenised digital rupee issued by RBI as a CBDC.
  • Chandigarh was an early adopter of food-subsidy DBT in September 2015.

Don't confuse Pilot began in Gujarat (February 2026); the PMGKAY launch was in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli (14 August 2026).

India’s Proposed ₹10 and ₹20 Polymer Banknotes Must knowfull text

  • RBI proposed one billion notes of each: 200 crore notes, face value about ₹3,000 crore.
  • Proposal under Sections 24 (denominations) and 25 (design, form, materials) of the RBI Act, 1934.
  • BRBNMPL, an RBI subsidiary, started procuring polymer substrate.
  • Australia first issued a polymer banknote in 1988; more than 60 countries use them.
  • Currency in circulation up 12% to ₹41.23 lakh crore (end-March 2026); ₹500 notes about 86% of value.
  • Printing cost fell nearly 24% to ₹4,875 crore in 2025–26.

Don't confuse Section 24 = denominations; Section 25 = design, form and materials.

Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Replaces the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 with a technology-neutral framework.
  • Lok Sabha passed it 5 August 2026, Rajya Sabha 10 August; assent 13 August 2026.
  • Bankers' books include records at off-site, virtual, cloud, backup and disaster recovery locations.
  • 'Banks' include post office savings bank and money order offices.
  • Certified copies are prima facie (first-look), not conclusive, evidence.
  • NBFCs, payment aggregators and fintechs covered only if notified or under another law.

Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026 full text

  • Introduced in Lok Sabha on 3 August 2026; replaces the 1959 Act (in force April 1, 1960).
  • ISI stays an institution of national importance under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
  • President of India would be the Visitor; can order reviews and nominate the Board Chairperson.
  • An 11-member Board would replace the 33-member Council.
  • Board: Chairperson, government representatives, four external experts and four ISI representatives.
  • The Director would be the Chief Executive Officer.

Memory aid 11 replaces 33: the new Board is one-third the size of the old Council.

VB – G RAM G Act, 2025 Must knowfull text

  • Full name: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025.
  • In force across rural India from July 1, 2026; repealed MGNREGA, 2005.
  • Guarantee raised from 100 to 125 days per year; wage floor ₹300/day for 2026–27.
  • Funding: 90:10 for Northeastern and Himalayan States; 60:40 for other States/UTs with legislatures.
  • Shivraj Singh Chouhan released over ₹25,000 crore as first instalment, the 'Mother Sanction'.
  • FY 2026–27 Central share ₹95,692.31 crore (Budget Estimate); total outlay over ₹1.51 lakh crore.

Memory aid VB-G RAM G = Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar And Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). Motto: 'Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi'.

Don't confuse Old MGNREGA guarantee = 100 days; new Act = 125 days. UTs without legislatures get full Central funding.

Provisional Estimates of Annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 2025–26 Must knowfull text

  • Released by MoSPI on June 5, 2026, with fourth-quarter (January–March) estimates.
  • Real GDP 2025–26: ₹323.12 lakh crore vs ₹299.89 lakh crore in 2024–25 (growth 7.7%).
  • Nominal GDP 2025–26: ₹346.36 lakh crore, growth 8.9%.
  • Real GVA growth 7.9%; nominal GVA growth 9.1% (2025–26).
  • Fourth-quarter 2025–26 real GDP growth estimated at 7.8%.

Don't confuse Full-year 2025–26 real growth 7.7% vs Q4 growth 7.8%; real GDP 7.7% vs nominal GDP 8.9%.

New GDP Series (Base Year 2022–23) Must knowfull text

  • New base year 2022–23 replaced 2011–12; released by MoSPI on 27 February 2026.
  • Q1 FY 2026-27 real GDP: ₹81.36 lakh crore, growth 7.8% (vs 6.9% a year earlier).
  • Q1 FY 2026-27 nominal GDP: ₹88.27 lakh crore, growth 10.3%.
  • Revised real growth: 2023-24 7.3%, 2024-25 7.2%, 2025-26 7.8%.
  • Q1 2026-27 growth: GFCF 11.9%, exports 12.0%, PFCE 7.1%.

Don't confuse New base year 2022–23; old base year 2011–12.

National Health Accounts Estimates 2022–23 Must knowfull text

  • Total Health Expenditure (THE) 2022–23: ₹8,81,359 crore = 3.37% of GDP; ₹6,373 per person.
  • Government Health Expenditure: ₹3,85,332 crore = 43.72% of THE, 1.48% of GDP.
  • Out-of-Pocket Expenditure: ₹3,82,629 crore = 43.41% of THE; ₹2,767 per person.
  • Current Health Expenditure 87.00% and capital 13.00% of THE; uses System of Health Accounts 2011.
  • By level of care (share of Current Health Expenditure): primary ~46%, secondary ~34%, tertiary ~15%.
  • In government current health spending, primary care took 51%.

Don't confuse Government share (43.72%) and out-of-pocket share (43.41%) are very close; government is slightly higher.

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code Completes 10 Years Must knowfull text

  • IBC enacted May 28, 2016; IBBI set up October 1, 2016.
  • Till March 31, 2026: 8,987 cases admitted, 7,102 closed, 1,419 resolution plans approved.
  • 4,099 companies rescued; creditors realised more than ₹4 lakh crore.
  • Realisation about 95% of fair value and about 167% of liquidation value.
  • FY 2024-25: banks recovered ₹1.04 lakh crore; ₹0.54 lakh crore (52.4%) via IBC.
  • Banks' gross NPA ratio (domestic): 2.15% on September 30, 2025.

10 Years of UPI Must knowfull text

  • Pilot launch: 11 April 2016; 10 years completed April 11, 2026.
  • Record 22.64 billion transactions in March 2026; 24.51 billion in August 2026.
  • Over 81% of India's retail payment volume in FY 2024-25.
  • FY 2025–26: 24,161.69 crore transactions worth about ₹314 lakh crore.
  • Around 85% of India's digital payments (FY 2025–26); about 49% of global real-time payments (2025).

Income-Tax Act, 2025 Must knowfull text

  • In force from 1 April 2026; replaces the six-decade-old Income-tax Act, 1961.
  • 'Tax Year' replaces 'Assessment Year' and 'Previous Year'.
  • CBDT notified the Income-tax Rules, 2026 to implement the Act.
  • Form 130 replaces Form 16 (TDS certificate issued by employers).
  • New Act: 536 Sections, 23 Chapters, 16 Schedules; TDS/TCS in sections 392,393 and 394.
  • New regime (AY 2026-27): zero tax up to ₹12 lakh; standard deduction ₹75,000 (was ₹50,000).

Don't confuse Form 130 is new; Form 16 is the old TDS certificate. Zero-tax limit ₹12 lakh (new) vs ₹7 lakh (old).

Report of the 16th Finance Commission (2026–31) Must knowfull text

  • Constitutional body under Article 280; 16th FC set up December 31, 2023 under Dr. Arvind Panagariya.
  • Report submitted 17 November 2025; tabled in Parliament 1 February 2026.
  • States' vertical share stays 41%; weights: income distance 42.5%, population (2011) 17.5%.
  • Total grants about ₹9.47 lakh crore for 2026–31; ₹7.91 lakh crore for local bodies.
  • Fiscal deficit: Centre to 3.5% of GDP by 2030–31; States' ceiling stays 3% of GSDP.
  • UP's share: 17.94% (15th FC) to 17.62% (16th FC), highest among States listed.

Don't confuse 41% = States' vertical share (unchanged); 42.5% = weight for income distance. The 16th FC dropped revenue deficit, sector-specific and state-specific grants.

B. Key Policy Documents/Events

National Social Assistance Programme Must knowfull text

  • NSAP launched 15 August 1995; helps poor elderly, widows, disabled and families losing a breadwinner.
  • Outlay ₹53,428 crore over five years (FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31).
  • Renamed: NSAP to Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana; IGNOAPS to PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana.
  • Disability pension: ₹375/month (age 0–79), ₹625/month (80 and above).
  • Disability threshold cut from 80% to benchmark disability of at least 40%; eligible from birth.
  • 3.20 crore beneficiaries across 36 States and UTs.

Don't confuse 80 appears twice: age 80+ gets ₹625; 80% was the old disability threshold (now 40%).

Vital Statistics of India Based on the Civil Registration System 2024 Must knowfull text

  • Released by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India on July 1, 2026.
  • Registration level 2024: births 99.1%, deaths 99.4% (2000: 56.2% and 48.7%).
  • Sex Ratio at Birth: 933 females per 1,000 males (excluding Sikkim).
  • Highest SRB: Arunachal Pradesh (1,050); lowest: Nagaland (806).
  • Registered births rose by 2,66,319 (about 1.1%) from 2023 to 2024.
  • Stillbirths fell 19.3% to 81,117; infant deaths fell from 1,45,992 to 1,20,992.

Don't confuse SRB 933 comes from registered events; do not work it out from the 52.5% male / 47.5% female split.

National Family Health Survey-6 Must knowfull text

  • Released May 29, 2026 by the Health Ministry; IIPS, Mumbai surveyed 6.79 lakh households in 715 districts.
  • 95.9% of pregnant women got antenatal care; first-trimester care 70.0% to 76.2%; at least four visits 58.5% to 65.2%.
  • TFR stayed 2.0 (urban 1.6, rural 2.1); institutional deliveries 88.6% to 90.6%.
  • Full vaccination (12–23 months) 83.8% to 87.1%; rotavirus 36.4% to 85.4%.
  • Stunting fell 35.5% to 29.3%; overweight/obese women rose 24.0% to 30.7%.
  • Women using internet 33.3% to 64.3%; spousal violence 29.2% to 22.3%.

Memory aid Women's internet use nearly doubled: 33.3 to 64.3.

Don't confuse NFHS-6 survey was done in 2023–24 but released in 2026; it is compared with NFHS-5 (2019–21).

Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2024 Must knowfull text

  • Released May 20, 2026 with the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality (2022-24).
  • Birth rate 18.3 (2014: 21.0); highest Bihar 26.8, lowest Andaman and Nicobar 9.9.
  • Death rate 6.4; highest Chhattisgarh 8.4, lowest Chandigarh 3.9.
  • IMR 24 (2014: 39); highest Chhattisgarh 36, lowest Manipur 2.
  • MMR 87 per 100,000 live births (2022-24) vs 130 in 2014-16.
  • Natural growth rate 11.9; Bihar 20.8 (high), Kerala 3.9 (low).

Don't confuse Chhattisgarh tops both death rate (8.4) and IMR (36). 3.9 is twice: Chandigarh's death rate and Kerala's natural growth rate.

MoSPI Launches New Logo and Mascot full text

  • New logo and mascot unveiled by MoSPI on 1 January 2026.
  • Ashoka Chakra = truth, transparency, good governance; ₹ symbol at the centre.
  • Logo message: 'Data for Development'; colours saffron, white, green and deep blue.
  • Mascot 'सांख्यिकी' to be used in National Sample Surveys by the NSS wing of NSO.
  • Finance Ministry unveiled a common logo for Regional Rural Banks on 18 December 2025.

National Conference on Agriculture for Kharif Campaign 2026 full text

  • Held May 28-29, 2026 at NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi.
  • Chaired by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
  • Agriculture Ministers from 22 States took part, called a historic first.

Cabinet Approves MSP for 14 Kharif Crops for 2026–27 Must knowfull text

  • CCEA chaired by PM Narendra Modi; Marketing Season 2026–27.
  • Biggest MSP rises: sunflower seed ₹622, cotton ₹557, nigerseed ₹515, sesamum ₹500 per quintal.

  • Highest MSP: sesamum ₹10,346, then nigerseed ₹10,052 per quintal.
  • Union Budget 2018–19 rule: MSP at least 1.5 times the all-India weighted average (A2+FL) cost.

Third Advance Estimates of Production of Major Agricultural Crops for 2025–26 Must knowfull text

  • Released May 27, 2026 by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
  • Foodgrains 376.563 million tonnes vs 357.732 million tonnes in 2024–25 (about 18.8 million tonnes more).
  • Rice record 154.024 million tonnes; wheat 120.657 million tonnes.
  • Sugarcane record 500.063 million tonnes; groundnut record 13.074 million tonnes; oilseeds 43.059 million tonnes.
  • UP first in rice (198.05), wheat (358.77) and sugarcane (2,296.99) lakh tonnes.
  • Other leaders: maize and pulses Madhya Pradesh; oilseeds Rajasthan; cotton Maharashtra; jute West Bengal.

Memory aid UP's triple crown: No. 1 in rice, wheat and sugarcane.

Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics (BAHS) 2025 Must knowfull text

  • Released November 26, 2025 (National Milk Day) by MoS Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel.
  • Based on the Integrated Sample Survey, March 1, 2024 to February 28, 2025.
  • Milk 2024-25: 247.87 million tonnes (+3.58%), India 1st; 485 g/day per person.
  • Eggs: 149.11 billion, India 2nd; meat: 10.50 million tonnes, India 4th.
  • Top States: milk – Uttar Pradesh (15.66%); eggs – Andhra Pradesh; wool – Rajasthan (47.85%).
  • Livestock GVA up about 195% (2014–15 to 2023–24); 31% of agricultural GVA.

Don't confuse UP is first in milk (15.66%) but second in meat (12.20%), behind West Bengal (12.46%).

D. Industrial Sector

Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Act, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Introduced in Rajya Sabha on 28 July 2026 by MSME Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi.
  • Rajya Sabha passed 3 August, Lok Sabha 7 August, assent 13 August 2026; Act No. 16 of 2026.
  • CPSEs must settle MSME invoices through TReDS (RBI-regulated invoice platform).
  • Mediation within 90 days; failed mediation goes to arbitration within 30 days.
  • Buyer challenging an award deposits 75%; court releases at least 50% after six months.
  • Memorandum filing free and voluntary; TReDS discounted invoices ₹40,000 crore (2021–22) to ₹3.47 lakh crore (2025–26).

Don't confuse Bill was introduced first in the Rajya Sabha (28 July), not the Lok Sabha.

Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) Must knowfull text

  • Cabinet approval July 15, 2026; MeitY notified it on August 21, 2026.
  • Outlay ₹62,500 crore; runs five years, FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.
  • Succeeds PLI-LSEM, which ended 31 March 2026.
  • Incentive 2.25% to 5% on sales; up to 1.5% extra for local sourcing; Indian brands 3% extra.
  • Electronics production: ₹1.90 lakh crore (2014–15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025–26, estimate).
  • Electronic goods: India's third-largest export category, USD 47.96 billion in FY 2025–26.

Startup India Completes 10 Years Must knowfull text

  • Launched 16 January 2016; 16 January declared National Startup Day in 2022.
  • Startups: fewer than 500 (2014) to more than 2 lakh (2026).
  • Unicorns: 4 to nearly 125; 49,429 entities recognised as startups in 2025.
  • DPIIT announced National Startup Awards 5.0 with 20 award categories.
  • States' Startup Ranking Framework 5.0: 34 States/UTs; Gujarat Best Performer in Category A.
  • Uttar Pradesh was a Top Performer in Category A, with Karnataka, Punjab and Tamil Nadu.

Don't confuse 'Best Performer' (Gujarat; Arunachal Pradesh and Goa in Category B) is above 'Top Performer' (UP, Karnataka, Punjab, Tamil Nadu).

Semiconductor Manufacturing Units Must knowfull text

  • Approved 5 May 2026 under the India Semiconductor Mission; investment about ₹3,936 crore.
  • Expected to employ 2,230 skilled professionals.
  • Includes India's first commercial Mini/Micro-LED display facility using Gallium Nitride technology.
  • Crystal Matrix Limited at Dholera; Suchi Semicon Private Limited at Surat (assembly and test).
  • ISM total: 12 approved projects; cumulative investment about ₹1.64 lakh crore.

India’s First Chip Fabrication Plant at Commercial Dholera SEZ Must knowfull text

  • Union Cabinet approved the Dholera fab project on February 29, 2024; SEZ notified April 9, 2026.
  • Area 66.166 hectares; capacity 50,000 wafer starts per month.
  • Investment ₹91,000 crore; about 21,000 jobs; an AI-enabled fab.
  • Earlier chip SEZs at Sanand, Gujarat: Micron, CG Semi and Kaynes Semicon.

Don't confuse Dholera = Tata's fab (makes chips); Sanand = Micron, CG Semi, Kaynes (assembly, testing, packaging).

Global Financial Centres Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Top four: New York, London, Hong Kong, Singapore.
  • Made by Z/Yen Partners (London) and China Development Institute (Shenzhen); twice a year since 2007.

India Electric Mobility Index 2025 Must knowfull text

  • IEMI 2025: second edition, released 16 September 2026, covers January–December 2025.
  • 16 indicators; weights: transport electrification 50%, charging infrastructure 30%, research and innovation 20%.

  • Uttar Pradesh scored 51 (Front Runner); 58 in transport electrification.

World Economic Outlook Report (October 2026) Must knowfull text

  • Released 13 October 2026; title 'Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices'.
  • World growth: 3.5% (2025), 3.1% (2026), 3.4% (2027).
  • India: 7.0% in both FY 2026–27 and FY 2027–28, raised by 0.5 percentage points.
  • India by calendar year: 7.4% (2026) and 7.0% (2027).
  • Global inflation: 4.7% in 2026, then 4.1% in 2027.
  • China 4.5% (2026); world average 3.2% for 2028–2031.

Don't confuse For India, IMF's '2026' column means FY 2026–27 (7.0%); calendar year 2026 is 7.4%.

Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released October 12, 2026 by UNDP and OPHI; 108 countries, 6.3 billion people.
  • 1.2 billion (18.9%) acutely poor; first rise since the index began in 2010.
  • 33 countries, including India, halved their MPI; China was fastest (2010 to 2014).
  • Lowest poverty: Serbia (MPI 0.000); highest: Chad (MPI 0.517, incidence 84.2%).
  • India (2019–2021 survey): MPI 0.069, incidence 16.4% (55.1% in 2005–2006).
  • India has the largest number of poor: 237.849 million (about 23.78 crore), a projection.

Memory aid MPI = 3 dimensions (health, education, living standards), 10 indicators; poor if deprived in at least one-third (33.3%).

India’s Foreign Exchange Reserves Scale Record High Must knowfull text

  • Week ended August 21, 2026: up $12.422 billion to $729.328 billion.
  • Previous record: $728.494 billion (week ended February 27, 2026).
  • Eighth straight weekly rise; about $63 billion added in eight weeks.
  • Foreign currency assets $591.333 billion; gold $114.218 billion.
  • SDRs $18.852 billion; reserve position with IMF $4.925 billion.
  • FCNR(B) deposits gave the largest share, $65.40 billion (2013 scheme: about $26 billion).

Index of Services Production (ISP) Must knowfull text

  • ISP: India's first high-frequency measure of short-term changes in formal services output.
  • Fills a gap: the Index of Industrial Production does not cover services.
  • Trial covered 19 sub-sectors (about 60% of services); no single overall ISP yet.
  • April 2026 leader: accommodation and food services, 37.2% year-on-year growth.
  • Fourteen sub-sectors had double-digit growth in April 2026.
  • Base year 2024–25, broadly aligned with the new CPI series (reference year 2024).

Don't confuse IIP measures industry; ISP measures services. ISP base year 2024–25; CPI reference year 2024.

Investment Friendliness Index Must knowfull text

  • Grew from the PM's call for an 'Investment-Friendly Charter' at NITI's Ninth Governing Council (July 2024).
  • Covers 28 States and eight UTs; 100-point scale; eight pillars, 84 indicators.
  • Heaviest pillars: Infrastructure 25%, Business climate 20%.
  • Top 5: Gujarat 56.6, Maharashtra 53.7, Tamil Nadu 53.3, Goa 53.1, Odisha 52.4.
  • Uttar Pradesh is among 15 Frontrunners (score 45–50).
  • Peer leaders: Uttarakhand 47.5 (hilly/NE), Goa 53.1 (UTs and city-States).

WEF Energy Transition Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released June 18, 2026 by WEF with Accenture; 120 countries, 44 indicators.
  • Top 5: Sweden 75.3, Finland 74.1, Denmark 72.6, Estonia 70.9, Norway 70.5.
  • India ranked 70th (score 54.9), up two places.
  • Global energy investment hit a record USD 3.3 trillion in 2025.

Performance Grading Index for Districts 2024–25 Must knowfull text

  • Released by Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education.
  • 782 districts; 600 points; 70 indicators in 6 categories.
  • 653 districts improved scores; Uttam-2 rose from 1 to 16; none reached Utkarsh (above 90%) or Uttam-1.
  • Top: Diu 469 (Uttam-2), Kolhapur 463, Barnala 461; Punjab and Kerala strong.
  • Kerala: all its 14 districts placed in Uttam-2 or Uttam-3.
  • Lowest: South West Garo Hills, Meghalaya (173); then West Khasi Hills (176).

Index of Economic Freedom, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Published by The Heritage Foundation, Washington, D.C.; first in 1995; 2026 is the 32nd edition.
  • 176 countries ranked (index covers 184 economies); 12 indicators in four policy areas.
  • Top 5: Singapore 84.4, Switzerland, Ireland, Australia, Taiwan.
  • India 132nd (score 52.5): 'Mostly Unfree' (50–59.9).
  • 'Repressed' (0–49.9): North Korea last, 176th (score 3.1).
  • Neighbours below 50: Pakistan 152nd, China 154th, Maldives 158th, Myanmar 164th.

Don't confuse India is 'Mostly Unfree'; Pakistan and China fall in the lower 'Repressed' group.

Fiscal Health Index 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released 11 March 2026 in New Delhi; second annual edition.
  • Five pillars: Quality of Expenditure, Revenue Mobilisation, Fiscal Prudence, Debt Index, Debt Sustainability.
  • Major State Achievers: Odisha, Goa, Jharkhand.
  • Front-Runners: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka.
  • Bihar moved up from Aspirational to Performer; Tamil Nadu slipped.
  • NE/Himalayan Achievers: Arunachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

Don't confuse Achievers are the top group; UP is a Front-Runner, not an Achiever. Punjab, Kerala and West Bengal are most debt-stressed.

Export Preparedness Index (EPI) 2024 Must knowfull text

  • Released 14 January 2026 by NITI Aayog; 4th edition (first EPI: August 2020).
  • Linked to USD 1 trillion merchandise exports by 2030 and Viksit Bharat @2047.
  • Pillars: Export Infrastructure 20%, Business Ecosystem 40%, Policy & Governance 20%, Export Performance 20%.
  • Large States top 5: Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh.
  • Small/NE States/UTs: Uttarakhand 1st, Jammu and Kashmir 2nd, Nagaland 3rd.
  • UP ranked 4th and first among landlocked States (ODOP, dry ports, logistics reforms).

Memory aid Business Ecosystem weighs 40%, double each of the other three pillars (20% each).
