A. Recent Astronomical Activities

JAXA Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission full text

  • Launched 20 October 2026 on H3 Flight No. 10 from Tanegashima Space Center, Japan.
  • Studies Mars's two moons, Phobos and Deimos; will return at least 10 grams from Phobos.
  • Arrival at Mars expected 2027; samples reach Earth in 2031; planned duration about five years.
  • Key question: are the moons captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars?
  • Carries 13 instruments; rover IDEFIX built jointly by France's CNES and Germany's DLR.
  • NASA gives MEGANE spectrometer, P-Sampler and Deep Space Network; NASA gets about 15% of samples.

Memory aid Timeline 27 → 31: reach Mars 2027, back home 2031.

Don't confuse Samples come from Phobos, not Deimos. JAXA's C-Sampler takes subsurface material; NASA's P-Sampler takes surface particles.

First GAGAN-Based Satellite Must knowfull text

  • DGCA supervised India's first Satellite-Based Landing System (SLS) approach in late June 2026.
  • Aircraft: IndiGo Airbus A321; used satellite guidance instead of an Instrument Landing System (ILS).
  • GAGAN = GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation; built by ISRO and Airports Authority of India.
  • Ground network: 15 reference stations (INRES), 2 master control centres (INMCC), 3 uplink stations (INLUS).
  • 3 geostationary satellites carry GAGAN payloads; 4 communication networks link the stations.
  • NavIC gives positioning and timing; GAGAN corrects GPS for precise aircraft landing.

Memory aid GAGAN ground count 15-2-3: 15 stations watch, 2 centres compute, 3 stations send up.

Don't confuse GAGAN only improves (augments) GPS signals; NavIC is India's own regional navigation satellite system.

SOLAR-1 full text

  • Operational on June 10, 2026; operated by NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration).
  • Its data goes to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) for forecasts and alerts.
  • SOLAR-1 = Space Weather Observations at L1 to Advance Readiness–1; earlier name SWFO-L1.
  • It orbits the Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1).
  • Launched September 24, 2025 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
  • Final engine burn on January 23, 2026, after about four months and nearly one million miles.

Memory aid SOLAR-1 sits at L1: both carry a '1'.

Don't confuse Launched in 2025 (September 24) but made operational in 2026 (June 10).

Chandrayaan-3 Hop Experiment Must knowfull text

  • Report shared May 18, 2026 on Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander 'hop' experiment.
  • Vikram reignited its engines and landed nearly 50 cm away, testing ascent for future sample return.
  • ChaSTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment) is a lunar thermometer, re-inserted into the regolith (moon soil).
  • Found a two-layer structure in the top 6.5 cm of soil at the post-hop site.
  • Soil gets denser and stickier with depth; craters made temperatures drop faster (shadowing effect).
  • The engine firing blew away the top 3 cm of regolith.

Memory aid Hop 50 cm, blew off 3 cm, found layers in 6.5 cm.

India’s First Orbital Data Centre Satellite Pathfinder Must knowfull text

  • Announced 4 May 2026: Pixxel–Sarvam strategic partnership for Pathfinder.
  • Pixxel will design, build, launch and operate it, and give the hyperspectral imaging payload.
  • Sarvam gives the AI backbone: India-built language models running on the satellite's GPUs.
  • Orbital data centre = satellites with data-centre-class GPUs that run AI in orbit (like edge computing).
  • Pathfinder is a single-satellite demonstrator, built at Pixxel's Gigapixxel facility (up to 100 units).

Memory aid Pixxel = pictures and the satellite body; Sarvam = the AI brain.

Artemis II Mission full text

  • Lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026; first crewed Artemis flight.
  • Crewed lunar flyby: humans near the Moon for the first time in 53 years.
  • Tested NASA's Space Launch System and Orion spacecraft; the crew named Orion 'Integrity'.
  • Orion's heat shield worked as expected; char loss much lower than in Artemis I.
  • The last crewed Moon mission before this was Apollo 17 in 1972, which landed.
  • Artemis III: listed for 2027 as a low-Earth-orbit test of SpaceX and Blue Origin landers.

Don't confuse Artemis II = flyby only (no landing); Apollo 17 (1972) = landing.

International Conference on Spacecraft Mission Operations, 2026 full text

  • Second edition, SMOPS-2026, held 8 to 10 April 2026 in Bengaluru.
  • Organisers: ISRO, Astronautical Society of India (ASI), International Academy of Astronautics (IAA).
  • Theme: 'Innovative Operations for Smart and Sustainable Space Mission Management – Next Generation'.
  • Inaugurated on 8 April 2026 by A. S. Kiran Kumar, former Chairman of ISRO.

Don't confuse SMOPS-2026 was the second edition, not the first.

New Telescopes in Ladakh Must knowfull text

  • NLST (National Large Solar Telescope): Merak near Pangong Lake, Ladakh; 2-metre class; studies the Sun.
  • NLOT (National Large Optical–Infrared Telescope): Hanle, Ladakh; 13.7-metre segmented primary mirror.
  • Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT), Hanle: 2-metre telescope; first light 26 September 2000.
  • HCT is operated remotely from CREST near Bengaluru; upgrade planned to a 3.7-metre telescope.
  • COSMOS-2 Planetarium: at Amaravati, implemented by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

Memory aid Merak = Sun (Solar telescope by Pangong Lake); Hanle = night sky (NLOT + HCT).

Don't confuse NLST (Solar) is at Merak; NLOT (Optical–Infrared) is at Hanle. One letter apart.

India’s first Private EO Satellite Constellation Must knowfull text

  • Agreement formalised January 21, 2026 by IN-SPACe under the EO-PPP programme.
  • Pixxel Space (Bengaluru) leads; members: Piersight Space, SatSure Analytics India, Dhruva Space.
  • First time a private consortium invests over ₹1,200 crore (over five years) in Indian space.
  • 12 EO satellites with panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and SAR (radar) sensors.
  • To be developed and operationalised by 2029 (official statement of August 12, 2026).
  • Aim: reduce dependence on foreign satellite data; serve climate and disaster work.

Memory aid '12' twice: 12 satellites for ₹1,200 crore.

Don't confuse 'Allied Orbits' (12-satellite EO constellation) is different from Pathfinder (Pixxel–Sarvam orbital data centre).

ISRO’s LVM3 M6 Mission Must knowfull text

  • Launched December 24, 2025 by ISRO/NSIL for AST SpaceMobile (USA).
  • BlueBird Block-2 weighed 6,100 kg: heaviest payload launched by LVM3 from Indian soil.
  • Largest commercial communications satellite in low Earth orbit (223 m2 phased array).
  • 104th launch from Sriharikota; ninth successful LVM3 mission; third dedicated commercial mission.
  • Aim: direct-to-mobile connectivity from space for ordinary smartphones.

Don't confuse Ninth successful LVM3 mission overall, but only the third dedicated commercial one.

India’s first LNG-powered train Must knowfull text

India’s First Hydrogen-Powered Train Must knowfull text

  • Inaugurated 17 July 2026 by PM Narendra Modi on the Jind–Sonipat section (Northern Railway), Haryana.

ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research Must knowfull text

Aarogya Manthan 2026 Must knowfull text

JAMA Blood Group in Humans full text

  • JAMA = 49th human blood group system, numbered ISBT 049.
  • Ratified at the ISBT Kuala Lumpur Congress 2026; announced September 14, 2026.
  • Found by UK and Israel researchers studying an Israeli woman and her brother.
  • Her antibody reacted with most people's red blood cells, but not with hers or her brother's.
  • JAMA is a separate antigen-based system, not a new type beside A, B, AB and O.

Don't confuse JAMA is a blood group system (the 49th), not a fifth blood type next to A, B, AB and O.

Bhutan Eliminates Dog Transmitted Human Rabies Must knowfull text

  • Validated by WHO on September 4, 2026.
  • Bhutan: first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to achieve this.
  • No human death from dog-mediated rabies since June 2023.
  • WHO lists Bhutan, Chile and Mexico as the three validated countries.
  • WHO criteria (2018): at least two years with no such deaths, plus capacity to stop re-emergence.
  • Dogs cause up to 99% of human rabies; global plan aims to end deaths by 2030.

Saushrutam 2026 full text

Aarogya Setu 2.0 Must knowfull text

  • Launched 29 June 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, by J.P. Nadda.
  • Redesigned as a Personal Health Record (PHR) app under ABDM.
  • The original Aarogya Setu was built during COVID-19 for contact tracing.
  • New features: ABHA creation, AI digitisation of lab reports, PM-JAY Wallet, empanelled hospital search.
  • Launched alongside: Ayushman App, NHCX, Ayushman Sarathi WhatsApp chatbot, e-Sushrut Clinic, UHI, BHTS.

Don't confuse Old Aarogya Setu = COVID contact tracing; Aarogya Setu 2.0 = personal health record app.

10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity full text

  • 10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity: Chandigarh, 30 April to 1 May 2026.
  • Organised by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; inaugurated by J.P. Nadda.
  • States and UTs showed health innovations and best practices.
  • Swasth Bharat Portal: one-stop platform putting national health programmes on one interface.
  • JANANI (Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care): ABDM-aligned RMNCH+A data platform.

Mission SEHAT Must knowfull text

  • SEHAT = Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation.
  • Launched 11 May 2026 in New Delhi by J.P. Nadda and Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
  • Joint mission of ICAR (agriculture research) and ICMR (medical research).
  • Goal: 'Healthy Food, Healthy Farms and a Healthy India'.

Memory aid SEHAT joins Farm (ICAR) with Health (ICMR): two 'IC_R' councils.

Takeda’s TAK-003 (Qdenga) Must knowfull text

  • Subject Expert Committee (SEC) under DCGI recommended TAK-003 (Qdenga) for ages 4 to 60.
  • Made by Takeda Pharma, a Japanese company.
  • Live-attenuated (weakened virus) vaccine for dengue serotypes 1, 2, 3 and 4; DENV2 backbone.
  • Schedule: 2 doses, three months apart.
  • NCVBDC: 2,89,235 cases and 485 deaths (2023); 1,21,824 cases and 131 deaths (2025).

Don't confuse Qdenga is the brand name; TAK-003 is the code; Takeda is Japanese.

SAHI & BODH Health AI Initiatives Must knowfull text

  • Launched 17 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit 2026.
  • SAHI = Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India: national guidance framework.
  • BODH = Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI.
  • BODH built by IIT Kanpur with the National Health Authority; tests AI models without sharing data.
  • Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog) launched the book 'AI-Preneurs of India' on 45 AI startups.

Memory aid SAHI = the rules (Strategy); BODH = the test (Benchmarking).

Don't confuse BODH (health AI, IIT Kanpur) is different from Bodhan AI (education, IIT Madras).

India’s first state-funded Bio-Safety Level-4 (BSL-4) laboratory Must knowfull text

  • Foundation stone laid 13 January 2026 by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
  • Location: Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC), Gandhinagar.
  • BSL-4 = highest level of biological containment, for deadly pathogens like Ebola, Nipah, Marburg.
  • India's only functional civilian BSL-4 lab now: National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune.

Don't confuse Existing civilian BSL-4 lab = NIV Pune; new state-funded one = GBRC Gandhinagar.

WHO Global Tuberculosis (TB) Report 2025 Must knowfull text

  • Released November 12, 2025; data from 184 countries and areas.
  • 2024: 10.7 million people got TB worldwide (131 new cases per 100,000).
  • India's share 25%, the highest; then Indonesia (10%) and Philippines (6.8%).
  • India's incidence fell 21%: 237 per lakh (2015) to 187 per lakh (2024); global fall only 12%.
  • India's TB mortality fell from 28 to 21 per lakh (2015 to 2024).
  • Treatment coverage rose from 53% (2015) to over 92% (2024); 26.18 lakh patients diagnosed in 2024.

Memory aid '21' twice for India: incidence fell 21%, and deaths are now 21 per lakh.

Don't confuse 21% = India's fall in incidence; 12% = global fall. India's share of burden = 25%.

HPV Vaccination Drive for 14-Year-Old Girls Must knowfull text

  • Launched 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, Rajasthan; covers all 36 States and UTs.
  • Target: girls aged 14; about 1.2 crore benefit every year (RGI 2021 estimate).
  • Single dose of 0.5 ml, intramuscular, in the left upper arm; free and voluntary with parental consent.
  • Campaign mode for three months (90 days), then on routine immunisation days.
  • Registration on U-WIN platform; vaccine stocks managed on the e-VIN portal.
  • Cervical cancer: second most common cancer among Indian women (GLOBOCAN 2022).

Memory aid HPV drive: age 14, one dose, 1.2 crore girls a year.

Don't confuse U-WIN = registration and records; e-VIN = vaccine stock and logistics.

Malaria Vaccine: AdFalciVax Must knowfull text

  • Developed by the Regional Medical Research Centre (RMRC), Bhubaneswar, of ICMR.
  • Recombinant multi-stage vaccine candidate against Plasmodium falciparum; aims to cut infection and community transmission.
  • By June 17, 2026: licensed to five Indian companies; still preclinical (TRL 4), not yet approved.
  • Stays effective up to 12 months at normal room temperature, so no costly cold chain is needed.
  • Estimated cost only ₹20 per dose, versus ₹250 to ₹830 for existing vaccines.
  • WHO-recommended vaccines now: RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) and R21/Matrix-M; India targets zero indigenous cases by 2027, elimination by 2030.

Memory aid AdFalciVax: ₹20 a dose, 12 months without a fridge.

Don't confuse AdFalciVax is only a candidate (preclinical); the vaccines already in use are RTS,S and R21.

D. Defence

Ahuti Mk II full text

  • Built by Apollyon Dynamics, Hyderabad startup from the BITS Pilani Hyderabad Campus ecosystem.
  • Recorded test speed 498 km/h; confirmed 29 August 2026, entry published 1 September 2026.
  • Beat the previous benchmark of 325 km/h by 173 km/h.
  • Production interceptors target about 400 km/h operational speed.
  • Founders: Jayant Khatri and Sourya Choudhury; ₹2 lakh prototype grant from BITS Pilani SOLVE.

Don't confuse 498 km/h = record by the test platform; about 400 km/h = target for production interceptors.

DRDO develops indigenous GaN technology full text

  • Agreement May 13, 2026: SAMEER and ISRO's ISTRAC; GaN chips from GAETEC, DRDO.
  • GaN (Gallium Nitride): semiconductor for high-frequency, high-power uses.
  • One 3.5 × 3 mm GaN chip can deliver up to 30 watts.
  • DRDO's SSPL makes 4-inch Silicon Carbide (SiC) wafers and GaN HEMTs up to 150 watts.
  • GaN-on-SiC MMIC production at GAETEC, Hyderabad; iDEX contract with Agnit Semiconductors.
  • Uses: radars, electronic warfare, communications, surveillance (ISR) and unmanned systems.

India’s first indigenous long-range attack drone KAL Must knowfull text

  • Developed by IG Defence, a private firm headquartered in Noida.
  • Flight trial at Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
  • KAL: long-range one-way attack system for autonomous strike missions.
  • Declared range up to 1,000 km; endurance 7-8 hours.
  • Maximum take-off weight 200 kg; carries a 50 kg high-explosive warhead.
  • Speed: cruise 160 km/h, maximum 200 km/h; flies up to 5,000 m above sea level.

Memory aid KAL: made in Noida (UP), tested at Pokhran, reaches 1,000 km.

INS Mangrol Must knowfull text

  • Commissioned 12 October 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai; presided by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan.
  • Third ASW-SWC (Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft) built by Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi.
  • Named after Mangrol town, Junagadh district, Gujarat; revives minesweeper INS Mangrol (M85), served till April 7, 2004.
  • Over 80% indigenous; Abhay sonar, torpedoes, Maareech torpedo decoy; waterjet propulsion.
  • ASW-SWC programme: 16 vessels, eight from CSL Kochi (Mahe class) and eight from GRSE Kolkata.
  • Mahe class commissioning: INS Mahe (24 November 2025), INS Malvan (22 July 2026), INS Mangrol.

Memory aid Mahe class, 1-2-3: Mahe (Mumbai) → Malvan (Karwar) → Mangrol (Mumbai).

Don't confuse Mangrol (Gujarat town; commissioned Mumbai) vs Malvan (Maharashtra town; commissioned Karwar).

India’s First Indigenous 350 kg-Thrust-Class Expendable Turbojet Engine full text

  • Designed by DRDO's Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE).
  • Industry partner: Azad Engineering, Hyderabad, which manufactured and assembled it.
  • Delivered to GTRE on July 22, 2026.
  • First indigenous expendable turbojet engine of the 350 kg thrust class.
  • Shows DRDO–private industry teamwork; may cut imports of compact propulsion systems.

IOL launches ‘GARUD full text

  • Launched August 13, 2026 at DPSU Bhawan, New Delhi, with Dr Garima Bhagat present.
  • IOL: Mini Ratna Category-I Defence PSU under the Department of Defence Production.
  • Made by Ordnance Factory, Dehradun, a unit of IOL.
  • Features: 8x magnification, 7.6-degree field of view, ±5 diopter, about 610 grams.

India’s first privately built FFSC rocket engine full text

  • Unveiled August 7, 2026 by Astrobase Space Technologies, Bengaluru.
  • FFSC = Full-Flow Staged Combustion: fuel and oxidiser go through separate pre-burners.
  • India's first LOX-methane high-thrust engine; fourth commercial FFSC globally (after SpaceX, Stoke Space, LandSpace).
  • Could support reusable launches of up to 30 tonnes to low Earth orbit.
  • As of August 22, 2026, full hot-fire testing was pending; figures are design targets.

Don't confuse Performance figures are company design targets; the engine was not yet fully hot-fire tested.

The Indian Navy launched Machilipatnam full text

  • Launched July 29, 2026 at Kochi by Mrs Goolrukh Anand; Vice Admiral Atul Anand present.
  • Yard number BY 529; seventh in CSL's eight-ship Mahe-class series.
  • Named after Machilipatnam, port city and HQ of Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.
  • Roles: coastal anti-submarine warfare, underwater surveillance, mine-laying; over 80% indigenous.
  • Contract for eight vessels signed April 30, 2019; whole programme: 16 ASW SWCs (CSL Mahe + GRSE Arnala).

Don't confuse 'Seventh' is its building order, not the seventh commissioned. Launched is not the same as commissioned.

INS Malvan commissioned into Indian Navy Must knowfull text

  • Commissioned July 22, 2026 at Karwar.
  • Second of eight ASW-SWCs built by CSL, Kochi; sixth of 16 ASW-SWCs commissioned.
  • Named after Malvan, a coastal town in Maharashtra linked to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
  • Crest: 'Bagh Nakha' (Tiger's Claw); motto: 'Silent Claws'.
  • Over 80 percent indigenous content.

Memory aid Malvan → Shivaji → Bagh Nakha (tiger's claw) → motto 'Silent Claws'.

Don't confuse Second of CSL's eight, but sixth of all 16 ASW-SWCs to be commissioned.

Garudastra Mortar System full text

  • Demonstrated June 17, 2026 at the Infantry School, Mhow, to the Indian Army.
  • Maker: Nibe Limited, Pune, with a foreign original equipment manufacturer (OEM).
  • A 120 mm mortar mounted on a mobile vehicle.
  • Shown on a No Cost–No Commitment (NC-NC) basis.
  • Offers fast mobility, high firepower, quick deployment and withdrawal.

ICGS Akshay Commissioned into Bharatiya Tatrakshak Fleet full text

  • Commissioned June 27, 2026 at Goa Shipyard Limited, Goa.
  • Type: new-generation Fast Patrol Vessel (FPV).
  • 'Akshay' means Indestructible.
  • Roles: law enforcement, coastal security, search and rescue, marine environment protection.
  • Designed and built by Goa Shipyard Limited: Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

Don't confuse Akshay = 'Indestructible' (June 2026); Achal = 'firm' (May 2026). Both are Goa Shipyard patrol vessels.

I-2SEA Submarine Cable System Unveiled full text

  • Consortium: Microsoft, Singtel, Tata Communications and Lightstorm.
  • Lightstorm announced construction contracts on July 2, 2026.
  • Links India's east coast to Singapore and Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur).
  • Two landings in India: Machilipatnam (shortest access to Hyderabad) and South Chennai.
  • About 3,600 km long from Singapore to Machilipatnam.
  • NEC Corporation is system supplier; ASEAN Cableship is marine installation partner.

India Becomes World’s Top Ship Recycling Nation in 2025 Must knowfull text

  • India's share of global ship recycling: 35.4% in 2025 (30.1% in 2024).
  • Data from UNCTAD, cited by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways on 22 June 2026.
  • Volume recycled: 2.99 million GT in 2025, up from 1.86 million GT in 2024.
  • Annual growth in recycling volume: nearly 60%.
  • Achieved a Maritime India Vision 2030 target five years ahead of schedule.

Memory aid 35.4% in 2025: 'thirty-five in twenty-five'.

Don't confuse 35.4% is the 2025 share; 30.1% is the 2024 share.

‘INS Mahendragiri’ Must knowfull text

  • Commissioned July 11, 2026 at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, into the Eastern Fleet.
  • Sixth Project 17A stealth frigate commissioned within about 18 months.
  • Named after the Mahendragiri range, Eastern Ghats; motto 'Mighty, Majestic, Matchless'.
  • Built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Mumbai; designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau.
  • Over 75 percent indigenous; about 6,670 tonnes; speed up to 28 knots.
  • Project 17A (Nilgiri class): seven frigates, four by MDL and three by GRSE; seventh is Vindhyagiri.

Memory aid Mahendragiri motto = three M's: Mighty, Majestic, Matchless.

Don't confuse Sixth Project 17A frigate commissioned overall, but the fourth built by MDL.

First EXIM shipping container manufactured in India Must knowfull text

  • Unveiled July 3, 2026 by Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.
  • Made for global shipping company A.P. Moller–Maersk.
  • Place: Maersk–CONCOR Inland Container Depot, Dadri, Uttar Pradesh.
  • Backed by the ₹10,000-crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (Union Budget 2026–27).
  • Plan: raise yearly container-making capacity nearly tenfold to around 7.5 lakh TEUs.
  • Also: ICGS Achal ('firm'), an Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessel, commissioned May 09, 2026 at Goa Shipyard.

Memory aid Dadri (UP) = first 'Made in India' export box, for Maersk.

Don't confuse ICGS Achal = 'firm' (Adamya class, May 2026); ICGS Akshay = 'Indestructible' (June 2026).

India’s 1st Indigenous Glide Weapon TARA Must knowfull text

  • TARA = Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation.
  • Maiden flight-trial by DRDO and the Indian Air Force off the coast of Odisha on 7 May 2026.
  • A modular range extension kit that turns unguided warheads into precision-guided weapons.
  • Designed by Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, with other DRDO labs.
  • Aim: raise the combat value of low-cost aerial weapons.

Oreshnik Ballistic Missile full text

  • Used by Russia on May 24, 2026 during a mass drone and missile attack on Kyiv.
  • Oreshnik means 'Hazel Tree': its warheads fall in streaks of fiery light.
  • Ukrainians called the first one fired 'Kedr' (Cedar).
  • Likely an intermediate-range ballistic missile; range 3,000 to 5,000 km.

Don't confuse Oreshnik = Hazel Tree (Russian name); Kedr = Cedar (Ukrainian nickname).

Delivery of Malwan full text

  • Delivered March 31, 2026 by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi.
  • Part of the Mahe-class ASW Shallow Water Craft project.
  • Named after Malwan, a historic coastal town in Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra.
  • Name reflects the maritime legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
  • ASW SWCs detect and counter submarines in littoral (near-shore) waters.

Don't confuse Delivery (31 March 2026) is not the same as commissioning.

Delivery of AGRAY full text

  • Delivered March 30, 2026 at Kolkata.
  • Fourth of eight ASW SWCs being built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata.
  • About 77 metres long; class called the largest Indian Naval warships propelled by waterjets.
  • GRSE also delivered Sanshodhak, the fourth and final Survey Vessel (Large), for hydrographic surveys.

Don't confuse Agray is built by GRSE (Kolkata), not by Cochin Shipyard like the Mahe-class ships.

Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile ‘Agni-III’ Must knowfull text

  • Test-fired February 6, 2026 from the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha.
  • Agni-III: indigenous, two-stage, solid-fuelled IRBM; range over 3000 km; 1.5-tonne payload.
  • Agni ranges: Agni-1 700 km, Agni-2 2,000 km, Agni-3 3,000 km, Agni-4 4,000 km, Agni-5 5,000 km.
  • Also: first Cadet Training Ship 'Krishna' (Yard 18003) launched 16 Feb 2026 at L&T, Kattupalli (Chennai).
  • Krishna is the first of three Cadet Training Ships.

Memory aid Agni ranges: 1 → 700 km, then 2, 3, 4, 5 → thousand km each.

Don't confuse Agni-III range is about 3,000 km; the longest is Agni-5 at 5,000 km.

INS Aridaman Must knowfull text

  • INS Aridhaman/Aridaman: India's third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (reported induction).
  • A larger vessel of about 7,000 tonnes.
  • Carries more K-15 missiles and K-4 SLBMs that can hit targets 3,500 km away.
  • Has nearly double the number of VLS tubes of its predecessors.
  • Stealth frigate INS Taragiri was officially commissioned at Visakhapatnam.

Don't confuse K-4 (range 3,500 km) and K-15 are submarine-launched missiles; Aridaman is the third such submarine.

Indigenous Pilot trainer Aircraft ‘HANSA-3 NG”, full text

  • Launched November 29, 2025 by Dr. Jitendra Singh, MoS (Independent Charge), Science and Technology.
  • Developed by CSIR–National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), Bengaluru.
  • All-composite airframe (not purely metal).
  • Meets demand for PPL (Private Pilot Licence) and CPL (Commercial Pilot Licence) training.
  • First designed by CSIR-NAL in the early 1990s; the new version is much upgraded.

Dhvani: Hypersonic Missile Must knowfull text

  • Developed by DRDO under its advanced hypersonic weapons programme.
  • Type: Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV).
  • Speed above Mach 5 (more than 7,400 km/h): current missile defences can hardly intercept it.
  • Can make sharp, high-speed changes of direction at high altitudes.
  • Possible range 6,000 to 10,000 kilometers: nearly double the reach of Agni-V ICBM.

Don't confuse Dhvani is a glide vehicle (HGV), not a ballistic missile like Agni-V.

‘Saksham’ Counter-Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS) Grid System Must knowfull text

  • SAKSHAM = Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard Kill Assets Management.
  • Indigenous C-UAS (counter-drone) grid system developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL).
  • Aim: detect, track, identify and neutralise enemy drones in real time in border areas.
  • Procurement started by the Indian Army to counter emerging aerial threats.

Memory aid SAKSHAM spelt out: Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard kill Assets Management.

E. Miscellaneous

Global Fintech Fest 2026 full text

  • 7th edition of the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) held in Mumbai, 8 to 11 September 2026.
  • GFF began in 2020; called the world's largest fintech festival.
  • Theme: 'Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum: Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance'.
  • Agentic AI: systems that sense, decide and act; Tokenisation: assets as programmable digital units.
  • India's fintech rise built on Aadhaar, UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).

Memory aid GFF 2026 theme = A-T-Q: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum.

Indian Telecom Services Performance Indicator Report 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Released by TRAI on October 12, 2026; covers 1st April 2026 to 30th June 2026.
  • Internet subscriptions: 1,092.79 million (March) to 1,114.17 million (June 2026), up 1.96%.
  • Total telephone subscriptions 1,348.08 million; tele-density 94.31 per 100 people.
  • Private operators hold 92.50% of telephone subscriptions; public sector 7.50%.
  • Monthly wireless ARPU up 1.19% to ₹187.12; rural share fell to 41.24%.
  • Mobile data use up 8.30% to 84,424 PB; 28.39 GB per subscriber per month.

Memory aid Tele-density 94.31: about 94 connections per 100 people.

Don't confuse Tele-density 94.31 includes machine-to-machine (M2M) links; without M2M it is 84.88.

Indigenous Micro Graphics Processing Unit at IIT Delhi full text

  • Announced September 24, 2026 by IIT Delhi.
  • Led by M.Tech students Nammi Akash and M. Ravi Teja under Prof. Jayadeva and Prof. Kaushik Saha.
  • Custom floating-point GPU engine, built fully in Register Transfer Language (RTL).
  • Shown on a Spartan-7 FPGA (chip programmable after manufacture); ASIC (task-specific chip) planned.
  • Targets embedded devices: computers made for specific jobs.

Don't confuse Demonstrated on an FPGA; the ASIC version is only planned.

NFI 2026 & Biovigilance Programme of India Must knowfull text

  • Launched 21 September 2026 by MoS Health Anupriya Patel at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.
  • Occasion: 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week, organised by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC).
  • Launched: 7th Edition of National Formulary of India (NFI), medical-device safety guidance, ADR-PvPI 2.0 iOS app.
  • Biovigilance Programme of India: monitors adverse events from products used in organ and tissue transplants.
  • Covers products given to both donors and recipients.

Don't confuse 7th = edition of NFI; 6th = National Pharmacovigilance Week.

Cabinet approves scheme of Chemical Parks (BHAVYA Rasayan) Must knowfull text

  • BHAVYA = Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana; Rasayan scheme for three Chemical Parks.
  • Announced in Union Budget FY 2026–27; approved by the Union Cabinet chaired by PM Modi.
  • Total outlay Rs.3,030 crore: Rs.3,000 crore for infrastructure, Rs. 30 crore administrative.
  • Runs for 5 years: FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
  • Centre gives up to Rs.1,000 crore per park; State must give at least Rs.500 crore.

Memory aid Three 3s: three parks, Rs.3,030 crore total, Rs.3,000 crore for infrastructure.

Don't confuse Rs.1,000 crore = Centre's maximum grant per park; Rs.500 crore = State's minimum share.

India commissioned its first and deepest geothermal wells Must knowfull text

  • Two 1000-metre-deep geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh: India's first, in the cold desert.
  • Altitude: 14,000 feet.
  • Inaugurated by VK Saxena, Lt Governor of Ladakh.
  • Will support a 1 MW pilot geothermal power project at Puga: India's first demonstration-scale project.
  • Maximum temperature of 135 degrees Celsius recorded at 400 metres depth.

Memory aid Puga: 2 wells, 1000 m deep, for 1 MW.

Don't confuse 135°C was recorded at 400 m depth, although the wells are 1000 m deep.

Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Held 19 to 22 March 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
  • Theme: 'Electrifying Growth. Empowering Sustainability. Connecting Globally.'
  • Released: National Resource Adequacy Plan; Transmission Plan for over 900 GW non-fossil capacity by 2035–36.
  • FY 2025–26: record non-fossil addition of 55.29 GW (solar 44.61 GW, wind 6.05 GW).
  • As of 31 March 2026: total capacity 5,32,740 MW; non-fossil share 53.2%.
  • FY 2025–26 energy deficit only 0.03%; peak deficit only 0.01%.

Memory aid 'One Nation – One Grid – One Frequency': the world's largest synchronous national grid.

Don't confuse 52,537 MW is capacity added only up to 31 January 2026; the full-year non-fossil addition is 55.29 GW.

Research Station: Approval for the Construction of Maitri II Must knowfull text

  • Approval announced in a Ministry of Finance press release on October 4, 2025.
  • Maitri II: India's proposed fourth research station, in East Antarctica; to be ready by 2032.
  • First station: Dakshin Gangotri; active stations: Maitri (since 1989) and Bharati (since 2012).
  • Maitri is on the Schirmacher Oasis, a 20 km ice-free stretch, about 100 km inland.
  • Project executed by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa.

Memory aid Antarctic line-up: Dakshin Gangotri → Maitri (1989) → Bharati (2012) → Maitri II (2032).

Don't confuse Maitri II will be the fourth station, though only two (Maitri, Bharati) are active now.

News in Short full text

  • NSHIP, TN (National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park): India's first SPV for a mega shipbuilding cluster.
  • WAVES Animation Bazaar and 8th India Joy 2025: two-day event inaugurated November 1, 2025, Hyderabad.
  • Supported by Telangana government, Telangana VFX, Animation and Gaming Association and Union I&B Ministry.
  • 11th India International Science Festival (IISF): December 6-9, 2025, Panchkula, Haryana.
  • IISF 2025 theme: 'Vigyan Se Samruddhi: for Atmanirbhar Bharat'.

Environmental Affairs (पर्यावरण परिदृश्य)

32 topics · 24 marked Must know · 49 practice questions

UNEP’s Emissions Gap Report 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Global emissions: 58.4 GtCO2e in 2025 vs a revised 58.5 GtCO2e in 2024; no confirmed peak.
  • Cuts needed from 2025 levels: 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040.
  • Full NDC implementation gives only 5–8% cuts by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035.
  • India: 4.5 billion tonnes CO2e in 2025, third after China and the United States (excluding LULUCF).
  • India per person: 3.1 tonnes vs global average 6.4 tonnes; lowest among six largest emitters.
  • India and China together hold 95% of coal-power capacity under construction worldwide.

Memory aid India: third in total (4.5 billion tonnes) but lowest per person (3.1 tonnes): big country, small footprint per head.

Don't confuse 58.4 Gt = 2025 global emissions; 58.5 Gt = revised 2024 figure. 76% appears twice: G20 share of emissions and share covered by 124 Parties' updated NDCs.

India’s Ramsar Sites Tally Reaches 103 Must knowfull text

  • 103rd: Sauj Lake, Mainpuri district, UP; Ganga floodplain, near Saman Bird Sanctuary.
  • 102nd: Sukhna Wetland, edge of Chandigarh, at the base of the Outer Himalayas.
  • 101st: Glaw Lake (Glaw Tuwi), Lohit district; Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar Site (3 August 2026).
  • 100th: Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal), Ballia, UP (5 June 2026).
  • Grew from 26 sites (2014) to 103 (2026); India third globally after UK (176) and Mexico (144).
  • Most sites: Tamil Nadu (20); largest: Sundarbans; smallest: Vembannur; first: Chilika and Keoladeo (1981).

Memory aid UP bookends: 100th (Surha Tal, Ballia) and 103rd (Sauj Lake, Mainpuri) are both in Uttar Pradesh.

Don't confuse Order: Glaw Lake = 101st (Arunachal) → Sukhna = 102nd (Chandigarh) → Sauj Lake = 103rd (UP).

India’s first petroglyph conservation park inaugurated in Leh Must knowfull text

  • India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park → Sindhu Ghat, Leh (Ladakh).
  • Inaugurated by PM Modi on October 15, 2026.
  • Petroglyphs are ancient rock carvings.
  • The open-air park protects carvings from erosion, infrastructure expansion and unregulated tourism.

Memory aid Petro = rock, glyph = carving: petroglyph = rock carving.

The Kigali Amendment marked its 10th anniversary Must knowfull text

  • Adopted at Kigali on October 15, 2016; entered into force in January 2019.
  • Aim: phase down HFCs; could avoid about 0.3–0.5°C of warming by 2100.
  • HFCs don't harm the ozone layer but warm hundreds or thousands of times more than CO2.
  • Called 'phase-down', not phase-out, because limited HFC use can continue.
  • India ratified in 2021: freeze by 2028, 10% cut by 2032, 85% cut by 2047.
  • Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs; nearly 99% of controlled ozone-depleting substances eliminated.

Memory aid India's Kigali ladder: 2028 freeze → 2032 cut 10% → 2047 cut 85%.

Don't confuse Montreal Protocol (1987) = ozone-depleting substances like CFCs (phase-out); Kigali Amendment (2016) = HFCs (phase-down).

Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme Must knowfull text

  • Approved by the Union Cabinet on 30 September 2026; target completion FY 2032–33.
  • Strengthens the Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) within States and Union Territories.
  • Supports evacuation of up to 135 GW renewable energy and 50 GWh battery storage (BESS).
  • Total outlay ₹1,86,405 crore: InSTS ₹1,36,378 crore; battery storage ₹50,000 crore.
  • Central Financial Support ₹54,082 crore, to lower intra-state transmission charges.
  • Supports India's target of 900 GW non-fossil installed capacity by 2035.

Memory aid Green Energy Corridor = a highway of power lines carrying green electricity from plants to the grid.

Don't confuse 135 GW = renewable power to be evacuated; 50 GWh = battery storage to be deployed.

India’s Net Zero Portal and the NAPCC Dashboard Must knowfull text

  • Launched 16 September 2026 in Mumbai by MoS Environment Kirti Vardhan Singh, on World Ozone Day.
  • Net Zero Portal: voluntary registration and disclosure of Net Zero commitments by Indian entities.
  • NAPCC Dashboard: single view of progress of National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
  • NDC for 2031–2035 (submitted 24 April 2026): 47% intensity cut, about 60% non-fossil capacity by 2035.
  • Early wins: 40% non-fossil target met in 2021, nine years early; 50% met June 2025.
  • Emissions intensity fell 37.38% by 2022 vs 2005; non-fossil about 55% of capacity (30 September 2026).

Memory aid Target ladders for 2015 → 2022 → 2026: non-fossil share 40 → 50 → 60%; intensity cut 33–35 → 45 → 47%.

Don't confuse The 2015 INDC and 2022 update targets are 'by 2030'; the 2026 NDC targets are 'by 2035'.

Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar 2026 full text

  • Fifth edition held 12 to 19 September 2026; launched on 1 September.
  • Meaning: Clean Coast, Safe Sea; led by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
  • Beach cleanups planned at 100-plus locations, with human chains, cycling rallies and marathons.
  • Included what MoES called the first national Ocean Olympiad for students and youth.
  • Campaign began on 5 July 2022; goals: consume responsibly, segregate waste at home, dispose responsibly.

Memory aid Three goals follow an item's life: Consume → Segregate → Dispose (all responsibly).

Don't confuse The campaign started in 2022; the 2026 drive is its fifth edition.

Project GIB Adds Three Chicks Must knowfull text

  • Announced by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on 14 June 2026.
  • Fourth breeding year: 26 chicks; 18 by artificial insemination, four natural, four from wild eggs.
  • Captive stock has grown to 94 birds.
  • Three chicks hatched in the wild in Rajasthan through a 'jumpstart' intervention.
  • Project launched by Rajasthan's Chief Minister on 5 June 2013, first in Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.
  • GIB (Godawan; Ardeotis nigriceps): Critically Endangered state bird of Rajasthan; grassland health indicator.

Memory aid 26 = 18 + 4 + 4 (artificial insemination + natural + wild eggs).

Don't confuse 26 = chicks hatched in the fourth year; 94 = total captive stock.

WWF Global Conservation Conference at Jaipur (Rajasthan) Must knowfull text

  • Inaugurated by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav at Jaipur on 21 September 2026.
  • Protected areas: around 750 earlier → more than 1,000 now.
  • Tiger reserves: 47 → 58; elephant reserves: 30 → 33.
  • Ramsar sites: 24 → 103.
  • WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature): independent body formed in 1961, based in Switzerland.

Don't confuse 58 = tiger reserves; 33 = elephant reserves; 103 = Ramsar sites. Don't mix them.

Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana Must knowfull text

  • PM-SSY pairs Floating Solar PV (FSPV) projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems (ESS).
  • Target: add 5,000 MW of floating-solar capacity across all States and UTs.
  • Aid: ₹1 crore per MW after commissioning; up to ₹50 lakh per feasibility study.
  • Floating-solar potential about 102.18 GWp (NISE); only about 700 MW operational at approval.
  • Expected: cut about 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year; 16,000–17,000 jobs.
  • Solar capacity rose over 58 times: 2.82 GW (March 2014) → 164.59 GW (31 July 2026).

Memory aid Surya (sun) + Sarovar (lake) = solar panels floating on lakes and reservoirs.

Don't confuse ALMM-enlisted module capacity crossed 200 GW (August 2026), but actual module manufacturing capacity was about 192 GW (June 2026); the source says they differ.

India launched its first-ever Guide to Grasslands Must knowfull text

  • Launched August 17, 2026 at an official side event of UNCCD COP17, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
  • Under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; published by ATREE.
  • Aims to stop grasslands, scrublands and ravines being wrongly called 'wastelands'.
  • Covers Himalayan and Terai grasslands, Thar and Banni, Deccan savannas, ravines, coastal and desert landscapes.
  • UNCCD COP17 ran 17–28 August 2026; theme 'Restoring Land, Restoring Hope'.
  • 2026 = International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (UNGA Resolution 76/253, 15 March 2022); FAO leads.

Memory aid ONEs = Open Natural Ecosystems: grasslands are 'ONEs', not wastelands.

Don't confuse The Guide was launched at UNCCD COP17 (desertification convention), not at a UNFCCC climate COP.

India’s First Dedicated Urban Night Safari Must knowfull text

  • Supreme Court permission (15 July 2026) is conditional, not a blanket environmental clearance.
  • Site: inside the 2,027-hectare Kukrail Reserve Forest, on Lucknow's outskirts.
  • Kukrail has UP's first gharial rehabilitation centre, set up in 1975.
  • Project cost ₹1,510 crore; spread over 855 acres.
  • Phase I: Night Safari and Eco-tourism Zone; Phase II: Day Zoo.
  • Billed as India's first dedicated urban night safari.

Memory aid Kukrail forest: 2,027 hectares, read it like the year 2027.

Don't confuse 2,027 hectares = whole reserve forest; 855 acres = project area (different units too).

Prakriti Café full text

  • Inaugurated by Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav on 22 July 2026.
  • Located at Ayush Bhawan, New Delhi.
  • A workplace food outlet that brings Ayush Ahaar principles into daily meals.
  • Promotes mindful eating and nutritious diets rooted in India's traditional knowledge.

Ethanol Blending in India Must knowfull text

  • E20 = 20% ethanol + 80% petrol; India first achieved 20% blending in 2025.
  • Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) runs 1 November to 31 October, since November 2023.
  • EBP launched 2003; 2018 Biofuels Policy aimed E20 by 2030; 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025–26.
  • E10 achieved in June 2022; phased E20 rollout began 6 February 2023.
  • Capacity grew from 421 crore litres (2014) to about 2,000 crore litres (2026).
  • Gains since ESY 2014–15: forex savings over ₹1.97 lakh crore; farmer payments over ₹1.66 lakh crore.

Memory aid E-number = ethanol %: E5 = 5%, E10 = 10%, E20 = 20%.

Don't confuse E85 is not 85% ethanol: in the US it contains about 51–83%, for flex-fuel vehicles.

Tamil Nadu’s 3D-Printed Artificial Reef pilot under PMMSY full text

  • Off Rameswaram, Ramanathapuram district; Phase II of Tamil Nadu's artificial-reef programme.
  • Supported under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
  • Each module weighs about 1 tonne; made by Chennai startup Tvasta (IIT Madras-incubated).
  • Partner: Visakhapatnam Regional Centre of ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute; led by Dr Joe K. Kizhakudan.
  • Complex shapes with crevices and folds, unlike reinforced-concrete reefs.
  • Funded by Centre and State in a 60:40 ratio.

Memory aid Matsya = fish: PMMSY money builds new homes (reefs) for fish.

Don't confuse Startup Tvasta is Chennai-based; the partner CMFRI centre is in Visakhapatnam.

Sustainable Development Report 2026 and SDG Progress in India Must knowfull text

  • Released by SDSN on June 23, 2026; India 94th of 169, score 68.3 out of 100.
  • India rose 18 places, from 112th (2015) to 94th (2026); China improved 14 places.
  • Of 75 indicators: 25 on track, eight moderately improving, 33 stagnating, nine decreasing.
  • SDG 2: only cereal yield (3.6 t/ha, 2023) on track; stunting fell 37.9% → 35.5%.
  • Child wasting rose 16.9% (2017) → 18.7% (2020); adult obesity 4.91% → 7.27%.
  • Globally none of 17 SDGs is fully on course; 2025 was 1.43°C above pre-industrial.

Memory aid 112 − 18 = 94: India climbed 18 places since 2015.

Don't confuse 169 appears twice: countries ranked and total SDG targets. India's trend shares use 75 indicators, not 169 targets.

Centre of Excellence on Human-Wildlife Conflict Must knowfull text

  • Inaugurated by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on July 10, 2026.
  • Location: WII–SACON (Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.
  • He also launched the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal.
  • Released first edition of 'Current Status of Human–Wildlife Conflict in India: An Overview'.

Don't confuse SACON is in Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) and is a research institute of the Wildlife Institute of India.

Namo Oxygen Parks full text

  • Inaugurated June 5, 2026 (World Environment Day) by Bhupender Yadav and Delhi CM Rekha Gupta.
  • 18 Namo Oxygen Parks opened across the national capital.
  • Part of the nationwide 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign.
  • Origin: in 2024 the DDA illegally cut over 1,100 mature trees in the Southern Ridge.
  • Southern Ridge: protected reserve forest called the 'lungs of the capital'.

Don't confuse 18 = parks opened in 2026; 1,100 = trees illegally cut in 2024.

E85 Fuel Rollout in India Must knowfull text

  • Launched by Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri on June 5, 2026 (World Environment Day), New Delhi.
  • E85 = 80–85% ethanol + 14–19% petrol, made for flex-fuel vehicles.
  • Flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs) run on E20 to E100; engine detects ethanol content automatically.
  • E85 is priced nearly ₹20 per litre lower than petrol.
  • FFVs on E85 can cut lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by around 61% vs petrol vehicles.
  • Blending rose from 1.53% (2014) to 20% (June 5, 2026), five years ahead of schedule.

Memory aid E85 launch day = World Environment Day (June 5).

Don't confuse E85 is a high-ethanol fuel (80–85% ethanol); E20 is the normal 20% blend.

Andaman & Nicobar Islands Set Guinness World Records Must knowfull text

  • Two underwater Guinness World Records set in May 2026 at Swaraj Dweep.
  • Swaraj Dweep was earlier known as Havelock Island (South Andaman).
  • First record: 'Largest flag unfurled underwater' (Indian Tricolour).
  • Second record: 'Tallest human stack underwater'.
  • Record holder: Andaman and Nicobar Administration; aim: scuba, marine and responsible adventure tourism.

Memory aid Havelock Island → Swaraj Dweep: old name, new name.

First International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels full text

  • Focus: reducing dependence on coal, oil and gas in a just, orderly and equitable manner.
  • Background: the COP28 Global Stocktake decision.
  • First principle: participation by those ready to move forward.
  • Second principle: implementation as the guiding star, based on shared scientific certainty.
  • Third principle: focus on solutions that support the transition rather than delay it.

Memory aid Three principles in three words: Ready, Implement, Solve.

Don't confuse Its background is COP28's Global Stocktake, not COP30.

India’s 1st Satellite-Tagged Ganges Soft-shell Turtle Must knowfull text

  • Released May 15, 2026 in the 1,302 sq. km Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam.
  • India's first satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle.
  • Species: Nilssonia gangetica; endangered; Schedule I under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
  • Identified by arrowhead-shaped markings on top of its head.
  • Five of India's soft-shell turtle species are known from the Kaziranga landscape.

Memory aid An arrow on its head points to the Ganges soft-shell turtle.

India Ranks Third Globally in Renewable Energy Installed Capacity Must knowfull text

  • IRENA end-2025: China 2,258.02 GW, USA 466.45 GW, India 250.50 GW, Brazil 228.20 GW.
  • IRENA's July 2026 revision moved India from 250.52 GW to 250.50 GW; rank unchanged.
  • MNRE, 30 September 2026: renewables 299.247 GW + nuclear 8.780 GW = 308.027 GW non-fossil.
  • Solar (171.051 GW) and wind (59.201 GW) lead India's renewable capacity.
  • 50% non-fossil capacity target met June 2025; share reached 54.18% on 30 June 2026.
  • FY 2025–26 generation: fossil 70.73%, non-fossil 29.27%.

Memory aid Top four order: China → USA → India → Brazil.

Don't confuse Capacity share is not generation share: non-fossil was 54.18% of capacity (June 2026) but only 29.27% of FY 2025–26 generation.

COP 15 of the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species Must knowfull text

  • CMS = Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, also called the Bonn Convention.
  • COP15: Campo Grande, Brazil, March 23–29, 2026; theme 'Connecting Nature to Sustain Life'.
  • 40 species, subspecies and populations added or upgraded in Appendices I and II.
  • CMS now covers over 1,200 unique species.
  • Brazil holds the CMS COP Presidency for the next three years.
  • COP16: Bonn, Germany, in 2029, marking CMS's 50th anniversary (signed at Bonn, 1979).

Memory aid Signed at Bonn in 1979 → back to Bonn in 2029 for its 50th birthday.

Don't confuse CMS COP15 (Campo Grande) is a wildlife treaty meeting, not the UN climate COP.

Project Him Sarovar full text

  • Launched April 10, 2026 by Vinai Kumar Saxena, Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh.
  • Water-security plan for Ladakh's cold desert: scientific snow harvesting, storing snowmelt and glacial melt.
  • Phase I: 50 water bodies (30 in Leh, 20 in Kargil), covering nearly 25% of villages.
  • By June 12, 2026, 5 reservoirs were complete; target 100 water bodies by next year.

Memory aid Him (snow) + Sarovar (lake) = lakes of stored snowmelt.

Don't confuse 50 = Phase I water bodies; 100 = target for next year.

IQAir World Air Quality Report 2025 Must knowfull text

  • Released March 24, 2026; 8th edition; covers 2025; 9,446 cities in 143 countries/regions.
  • Only 13 countries, regions and territories met WHO's annual PM2.5 guideline of 5 μg/m³.
  • Only 14% of global cities met the guideline in 2025, down from 17% in 2024.
  • Most polluted city: Loni, India (112.5 μg/m³); Delhi city fourth (99.6).
  • Most polluted country: Pakistan (67.3); India sixth (48.9).
  • Most polluted capital: New Delhi (82.2), then Dhaka (68.0) and Dushanbe (57.3).

Memory aid New Delhi tops the capitals at 82.2 while the WHO guideline is just 5.

Don't confuse Loni, not Delhi, is the most polluted city (Delhi city is fourth); New Delhi tops only the capitals list. Also 13 = countries meeting the WHO guideline; 14% = share of cities.

India’s National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna Must knowfull text

  • Designated on March 24, 2026 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
  • Bhavasagara Referral Centre is at CMLRE (Centre for Marine Living Resources & Ecology), Kochi, Kerala.
  • CMLRE works under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
  • Stores deep-sea animal collections from India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
  • Holds over 3560 identified, geo-referenced voucher specimens; supports deep-sea taxonomy training.

Don't confuse Designated by MoEFCC, but CMLRE itself functions under MoES.

State of India’s Environment (SOE) 2026 Report Must knowfull text

  • Released by CSE and Down to Earth, February 25, 2026, at Anil Agarwal Dialogue, Nimli, near Alwar.
  • Jan 1–Nov 30, 2025: extreme weather on 99% of days; 4,419 deaths; 17.41 million hectares crops hit.
  • 2024: 88% of days, 3,393 deaths; 2023: 89% of days, 3,208 deaths.
  • Worst-hit states: Himachal Pradesh (267 days), Kerala (173), Madhya Pradesh (162).
  • Only 15% of Indians (about 200 million) live within 10 km of a continuous air monitor.
  • Ocean acidity has risen 30–40% since the industrial era.

Memory aid Extreme-weather days: 89% (2023) → 88% (2024) → 99% (2025), almost every day of 2025.

Don't confuse The SOE series began in 2014; CSE's Citizen's First Report dates to 1982.

International Renewable Energy Agency full text

  • Sixteenth Session of the IRENA Assembly concluded on 12 January 2026.
  • Venue: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
  • Theme: 'Powering Humanity: Renewable Energy for Shared Prosperity'.
  • IRENA Youth Forum on the sidelines: young leaders from more than 60 countries.

India’s First Indigenous Designed Pollution Control Vessel Must knowfull text

  • Commissioned by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh in Goa on January 05, 2026.
  • First of two Pollution Control Vessels built by Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL).
  • India's first indigenously designed pollution control vessel; over 60% indigenous content.
  • Largest ship in the Indian Coast Guard fleet to date.
  • Built mainly for pollution control, but its role is wider.

Don't confuse It is an Indian Coast Guard Ship (ICGS), not an Indian Navy ship (INS).

Global Methane Status Report full text

  • Launched 17 November 2025 during COP30 in Belém, Brazil.
  • UNEP says the GMP includes 159 countries plus the European Commission.
  • As of April 2025, GMP members covered about 57% of global human-caused methane emissions.
  • Sector shares: agriculture about 42%, energy 38%, waste 20%.
  • G20+ countries: about 65% of emissions and 72% of technical mitigation potential by 2030.

Memory aid Methane 42-38-20: Agriculture > Energy > Waste.

Don't confuse 57% = share covered by GMP members; 65% = share emitted by G20+ countries.

30th Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC: COP30 Must knowfull text

  • Held in Belém, Amazon region, November 10-22, 2025; an 'implementation-first' COP.
  • Belém Package: around 29 decisions as an implementation toolkit, based on the Global Mutirão decision.
  • Two-year Climate Finance Work Programme launched; Paris Agreement Article 9.1 reading strengthened.
  • Tropical Forest Forever Facility: Brazil-led, targets USD 125 billion; pays for protecting tropical forests.
  • Belém 4x Pledge: quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035 vs 2024; 23 countries endorsed; IEA tracks.
  • India: climate finance a legal obligation, demanded USD 1.3 trillion/year; opposed EU's CBAM.

Memory aid Mutirão (Brazil) ≈ Shramdaan (India): a community coming together for shared work.

Don't confuse Belém Health Action Plan = first international climate adaptation plan only for health (USD 300 million); Belém Action Mechanism = just transition. Don't mix.

Paddy Procurement Policy, 2026–27 Must knowfull text

  • MSP: ₹2,441/quintal for common paddy; ₹2,461/quintal for Grade-A.
  • Target 65 lakh metric tonnes; about 4,500 centres; eight procurement agencies.
  • Western UP: October 12, 2026 – February 15, 2027.
  • Eastern UP: November 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027.
  • Farmers to be paid within 48 hours.

Coarse Cereals Procurement Policy, 2026–27 Must knowfull text

  • Procurement period: 1 October to 31 December 2026.
  • MSP per quintal: maize ₹2,410, bajra ₹2,900, hybrid jowar ₹4,023, Maldandi jowar ₹4,073.
  • Targets: bajra 2.20 lakh MT, jowar 50,000 MT, maize 15,000 MT.

Uttar Pradesh Interest Waiver Scheme, 2026 Must knowfull text

  • Approved 9 October 2026; notified 16 October 2026.
  • Covers eligible tax demands outstanding up to 31 December 2025.
  • Interest waiver: 100% for dues up to ₹10 lakh; 90% for ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore.
  • 75% for ₹1–5 crore; 50% for dues above ₹5 crore.
  • Open in 75 districts for 3 months; eligible penalties fully waived.

Memory aid Bigger the due, smaller the waiver: 100 → 90 → 75 → 50.

National Military Drone Technology Hub, IIT Kanpur Must knowfull text

Reservation for Former Agniveers Must knowfull text

Uttar Pradesh Artificial Intelligence Mission (UP-AIM) Must knowfull text

  • Outlay ₹2,000 crore (2026–27 to 2030–31); ₹225 crore for 2026–27.

UP Startup Procurement Scheme, 2026 Must knowfull text

Uttar Pradesh Launches Neem Karoli Baba Spiritual Tourism Circuit Must knowfull text

  • Neem Karoli Ashram: Farrukhabad.
  • Hanuman Setu Temple: Lucknow.

Uttar Pradesh Budget 2026–27

Uttar Pradesh Budget 2026–27 Must knowfull text

  • Presented by Finance Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna on February 11, 2026.
  • Large, expansionary budget: growth, infrastructure, welfare, technology.
  • Continues the revenue surplus.
  • Fiscal deficit kept at 3% of GSDP.

Economic Background of Uttar Pradesh Must knowfull text

  • GSDP 2026–27 (current prices): ₹39.8 lakh crore, up 28% over 2025–26 RE.
  • 2024–25 GSDP growth (constant prices): 9%, vs India's 6.5% GDP growth.
  • 2024–25 structure: agriculture 27%, manufacturing 26%, services 47%.
  • Per capita GSDP 2024–25: ₹1,24,366 (+11.6%); India's per capita GDP ₹2,34,859.

Memory aid UP's per capita GSDP is about half of India's: ₹1,24,366 vs ₹2,34,859.

Overall Size of the Budget Must knowfull text

  • Total expenditure 2026–27: ₹9,12,696 crore (27% above 2025–26 RE).
  • Debt repayment ₹61,795 crore; net expenditure ₹8,50,901 crore.
  • Total receipts ₹8,48,233 crore; receipts excluding borrowings ₹7,32,420 crore.
  • The gap is partly met through borrowings.

Budget at a Glance Must knowfull text

  • Total expenditure 2026–27 BE: ₹9,12,690.35 crore (2025–26 RE: ₹7,16,230.95 crore).
  • Total receipts 2026–27 BE: ₹8,48,233.18 crore.
  • Fiscal deficit 2026–27 BE: ₹1,18,480.58 crore; capital expenditure ₹2,48,225.80 crore.
  • Rupee comes in: State's own tax revenue 39%, share in central tax 31.4%.
  • Rupee goes out includes interest payment 7.6% and subsidy 4.7%.

Revenue Surplus, Fiscal Deficit, and Primary Deficit Must knowfull text

  • Revenue surplus 2026–27: ₹64,458 crore = 1.6% of GSDP.
  • 2025–26 RE surplus was bigger: ₹74,348 crore (2.4% of GSDP).
  • Fiscal deficit 2026–27: ₹1,18,481 crore = 3% of GSDP.
  • 3% matches the 16th Finance Commission's limit for States (2026–31).
  • Primary deficit ₹49,560 crore = 1.2% of GSDP.

Don't confuse UP has a revenue surplus (1.6%) and a fiscal deficit (3%) at the same time.

Expenditure Pattern Must knowfull text

  • Revenue expenditure: ₹6,64,471 crore, 31% above 2025–26 RE.
  • Revenue spending covers salaries, pensions, interest, grants and subsidies.
  • Capital outlay: ₹1,77,744 crore, up 11%; creates roads, buildings, infrastructure.
  • Drivers: pension, general education, rural development, local body grants, energy.

Don't confuse Revenue expenditure grows faster (31%) than capital outlay (11%).

Receipts Structure Must knowfull text

  • Revenue receipts: ₹7,28,928 crore, 26% above 2025–26 RE.
  • About 50% from the State's own resources, 50% from the Centre.
  • Own tax revenue ₹3,34,491 crore (48% higher).
  • Own non-tax revenue ₹26,754 crore, almost double.
  • Share in central taxes ₹2,68,911 crore; central grants ₹98,772 crore.

Tax Revenue and Tax Trends Must knowfull text

  • State GST: ₹1,49,956 crore = 45% of own tax revenue; 79% above RE.
  • State excise: ₹71,278 crore (17% higher).
  • Sales tax/VAT: ₹48,115 crore (43% higher).
  • Stamp duty and registration: ₹43,802 crore; vehicle taxes ₹15,808 crore.
  • Most 2025–26 own-tax heads fell short of budget estimates.

Debt, Liabilities, and Guarantees Must knowfull text

  • Outstanding liabilities, end-2026–27: 23.1% of GSDP.
  • 2025–26 RE: 27.6% of GSDP.
  • Outstanding guarantees (31 March 2025): ₹1,71,924 crore = 5.8% of GSDP.
  • Guarantees are contingent liabilities that may become real obligations.

Sector-Wise Expenditure Priorities Must knowfull text

  • Listed sectors = 60% of total sectoral spending.
  • Education, Sports, Arts and Culture: ₹1,08,154 crore (28% higher).
  • Energy ₹56,621 crore; Health and Family Welfare ₹53,326 crore.
  • Transport ₹50,391 crore; Rural Development ₹49,044 crore (up 59%).
  • Police ₹41,898 crore; Agriculture ₹30,938 crore; Urban Development ₹27,532 crore.

Don't confuse Biggest allocation = Education (₹1,08,154 crore); biggest growth = Rural Development (59%).

  • Public debt-to-GDP: 29.3% (2016–17) to 28.0% (2024–25).
  • Far below the national level (81.3%) and global average (92.8%).

Per Capita Income Must knowfull text

  • Per capita income (net): ₹54,564 (2016–17) to ₹1,09,844 (2024–25).
  • CAGR about 9.1%; 14.7% during 2020–21 to 2024–25.
  • Per capita income (gross) 2024–25: ₹1,26,304.

Memory aid Net per capita income roughly doubled: ₹54,564 to ₹1,09,844.

Don't confuse 2024–25 net per capita income ₹1,09,844 vs gross ₹1,26,304.

Population and Demographic Trends Must knowfull text

  • UP population (March 2026 estimate): 25.19 crore.
  • 17.8% of India's 141.51 crore; 3.0% of the world's 830 crore.
  • India is about 17% of the world population.
  • As a country, UP would be 5th: after India, China, USA (33.5 crore), Indonesia (27.7 crore).

Population Growth and Fertility Must knowfull text

  • Population growth rate: 1.85% (2011) to 1.70% (2021).
  • Expected 0.58% a year during 2026–2051.
  • TFR: 2.7 (NFHS-4, 2015–16) to 2.4 (NFHS-5, 2019–21).
  • Expected to reach replacement level of 2.1 soon.

Life Expectancy and Social Indicators full text

  • Males: 62.5 years (2011) to 73.2 years (2051).
  • Females: 65.0 years (2011) to 77.1 years (2051).
  • Women live longer than men in both years.

Sex Ratio and Age Structure full text

  • Sex ratio at birth 2011: 111 boys per 100 girls.
  • 2011 pyramid: wide base (many children).
  • 2026: more working-age people (20–34 years).
  • 2046: fewer 0–14 year olds; more people aged 40 and above.

Dependence on Central Taxes Must knowfull text

  • Dependence on central taxes: 56.0% (2016–17) to 46.4% (2025–26, estimate).
  • Own tax revenue: ₹0.86 lakh crore (2016–17) to ₹2.09 lakh crore (2024–25, advance).
  • Capital expenditure: ₹69.79 to ₹147.72 thousand crore (2016–17 to 2024–25).
  • Public debt-to-GDP: 29.3% to 28.0%; national about 81.3%, global about 92.8%.

Budget and Receipts full text

  • Total budget: CAGR about 10.3%; about ₹8.09 lakh crore in 2025–26.
  • Total receipts: 10.2% CAGR, about ₹7.79 lakh crore.
  • 2025–26 revenue expenditure: ₹5.83 lakh crore.
  • Nine-year CAGR: revenue receipts 11.1%; revenue expenditure 11.9%.
  • Revenue expenditure/receipts: 92% (2016–17), 89.2% (2024–25), 87.9% (2025–26).

Composition of Revenue Receipts full text

  • Revenue receipts = income from regular government operations.
  • Parts: State's own resources (tax, non-tax) and Central transfers (divisible pool share, grants).
  • ₹2.57 lakh crore (2016–17) to ₹6.63 lakh crore (2025–26 BE).
  • Nine-year CAGR: own revenue 12%; central transfers 10.3%.

Breakup of Revenue full text

  • State tax revenue: ₹0.86 lakh crore (2016–17) to ₹2.95 lakh crore (2025–26); CAGR 14.7%.
  • Share in central taxes 2025–26: ₹2.55 lakh crore; growth 9.9%.
  • State non-tax revenue 2025–26: ₹0.25 lakh crore.
  • Central grants: CAGR 11.7%, to about ₹0.88 lakh crore (2025–26).

Don't confuse Own tax revenue grew fastest (14.7%), ahead of grants (11.7%) and central tax share (9.9%).

Bihar Budget 2026–27

Bihar Budget 2026–27 full text

  • Bihar Budget 2026–27 presented on February 3, 2026.
  • Presented by Finance Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav.
  • It is the state budget for the year 2026–27.

Key Highlights full text

  • Budget size: ₹23,885 crore (2004–05) → ₹3,47,589.76 crore (2026–27, including debt repayment).
  • Shows more spending power for social sectors, infrastructure and welfare.
  • After Saat Nischay-1 and -2, Saat Nischay-3 framed for 2025–2030.
  • Aim: take Bihar into the category of developed states.

Overall Budget Size and Fiscal Framework full text

  • Net expenditure ₹3,47,589.76 crore; ₹30,694.74 crore above 2025–26 BE (₹3,16,895.02 crore).
  • Scheme outlay ₹1,22,155.42 crore (35.14%); establishment/committed ₹2,25,434.34 crore (64.86%).
  • GSDP 2026–27 projected at about ₹13.09 lakh crore, about 15% growth.
  • Revenue surplus ₹1,143.19 crore; fiscal deficit ₹39,111.80 crore = 2.99% of GSDP.
  • Debt repayment about ₹22,665 crore; spending excluding it ₹3,24,925 crore.
  • Appropriation Bill gross ₹3,53,045.15 crore: voted ₹3,02,242.13 crore, charged ₹50,803.02 crore.

Memory aid 35.14 + 64.86 = 100: scheme vs committed spending.

Don't confuse Fiscal deficit is 2.99% of GSDP (within the 3% limit), yet the budget still shows a revenue surplus.

Revenue Receipts and Borrowings full text

  • Revenue receipts ₹2,85,277.12 crore: own sources ₹75,202.99 crore; Centre about ₹2,10,074 crore.
  • Own tax revenue ₹65,800 crore; State GST is the largest source at ₹38,000 crore.
  • Commercial taxes ₹50,000 crore; stamps and registration ₹10,000 crore; transport tax ₹5,000 crore.
  • Own non-tax revenue ₹9,402.99 crore, including ₹4,200 crore from mining.
  • Share in central taxes ₹1,58,178.32 crore; central grants ₹51,895.81 crore.
  • Borrowing proposed ₹61,939.48 crore; debt repayment ₹22,664.83 crore.

Don't confuse ₹1,58,178.32 crore = share in central taxes; ₹51,895.81 crore = grants-in-aid. Together about ₹2,10,074 crore from the Centre.

Capital and Revenue Expenditure full text

  • Capital expenditure ₹63,455.84 crore = 18.26% of total spending.
  • Capital outlay ₹39,377.06 crore; economic services largest at ₹25,824.96 crore.
  • Revenue expenditure ₹2,84,133.92 crore = 81.74% of total.
  • Salaries, pensions, interest and debt repayment together: ₹1,79,327.48 crore.
  • Committed spending (salaries, pensions, interest) ₹1,33,494 crore = 47% of revenue receipts.

Memory aid 18.26 + 81.74 = 100: capital + revenue spending.

  • 2024–25 shares: agriculture 22.37%, manufacturing 23.57%, services 54.07%.
  • Per capita GSDP 2024–25: ₹76,490 vs India's per capita GDP ₹2,34,859.
  • Per capita NSDP 2024–25: ₹69,321, up 11.45%.

  • Total expenditure ₹1.66 lakh crore (2020–21) → ₹2.82 lakh crore (2024–25).

  • Social services have the largest share of revenue expenditure: 46%.
  • Developmental expenditure: 67.4% of total in 2024–25 (₹1,89,892 crore).
  • Outstanding debt on 31 March 2025: ₹3,74,134 crore = 37.7% of GSDP.

Don't confuse 37.7% = debt-to-GSDP ratio; 67.4% = developmental share of spending.

Agriculture and Allied Sector full text

  • 2023–24: agriculture, forestry, fisheries = 23.1% of GSVA (crops 11.5%, livestock 8.1%).
  • 2024–25 cereal shares: rice 40.7%, wheat 32.1%, maize 27.1%.
  • Growth 2023–24 to 2024–25: rice 4.3%, wheat 7.1%, maize 12.6%.
  • Horticulture 2023–24: about 230 lakh tonnes (206 lakh tonnes in 2019–20).
  • Agriculture's share of electricity use: 5.3% (2020–21) → 14.9% (2024–25).
  • Kisan Credit Card credit up 32.8%: ₹7,080.07 crore → ₹9,399.24 crore.

Memory aid Cereal shares 40.7 + 32.1 + 27.1 = 99.9%: rice, wheat, maize make nearly all of it.

Enterprise Sector full text

  • Secondary sector fell sharply in 2020–21 (pandemic) and recovered in 2021–22.
  • Rapid growth in 2022–23, led by mining, utilities and construction.
  • 2024–25: 37.8 lakh tourists at 28 eco-tourism sites, 24.0% more than the year before.
  • Eco-tourism and park development outlay in 2024–25: ₹100.00 crore.

Human Development full text

  • Social services spending up 15-fold (2005–06 to 2024–25); health 14.8 times, education 13.2 times.
  • Life expectancy 2019–2023: males 68.9 years, females 69.7 years.
  • IMR fell 12 points, from 35 (2017) to 23 (2023).
  • MMR fell 208 points: 312 (2004–2006) → 104 (2021–2023).
  • Institutional deliveries (Janani Suraksha Yojana): 15.77 lakh → 16.17 lakh (up 2.54%).
  • Elementary enrolment 2024–25: 159.22 lakh (80.87 lakh boys, 78.35 lakh girls).

Memory aid 312 − 208 = 104 (MMR); 35 − 12 = 23 (IMR).

Environment, Climate Change and Disaster Management full text

  • Forestry and logging grew 10.4% a year (2011–12 to 2024–25): ₹4,187 → ₹15,139 crore.
  • Forest and tree cover: 9,214 → 9,903 sq km by 2023 (up 689 sq km).
  • Very dense forest rose from 231 to 387 sq km.
  • Power capacity 11,764 MW: thermal 7,743 MW; solar 1,922 MW is the largest renewable.
  • Credit-to-GSDP ratio rose 30.9% → 37.9% (2020–21 to 2024–25).
  • Bank NPAs fell from 11.8% to 7.6% over the same period.

Don't confuse Solar (1,922 MW) is the largest renewable source, ahead of hydropower (1,356 MW) and wind (699 MW).

Narendra Modi Must knowfull text

  • June 10, 2026: became longest-serving elected PM for consecutive terms, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Nehru first took oath as elected PM on May 13, 1952 and served until May 27, 1964.
  • Modi's continuous PM tenure, May 26, 2014 to June 10, 2026: 4399 days.
  • March 22, 2026: longest-serving head of an elected government (CM + PM combined): 8,931 days.
  • Uzbekistan's 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order (Order of Highest Friendship) from President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, August 30, 2026.
  • 2026 honours: Indonesia's Bintang Adipurna, Seychelles' Guardian of the Blue Horizon (first time given), FAO's Agricola Medal.
  • Also: Royal Norwegian Order of Merit, Sweden's Royal Order of the Polar Star, Israel's Medal of the Knesset.

Memory aid Award-country pairs: Bintang Adipurna = Indonesia; Blue Horizon = Seychelles; White Double Cross = Slovakia; Polar Star = Sweden; Knesset = Israel; Nishan = Ethiopia; Agricola = FAO.

Don't confuse Two different records: 4399 days = continuous PM tenure; 8,931 days = CM + PM tenure combined.

Don't confuse Glasgow hosted in 2014 and 2026; Edinburgh hosted in 1970 and 1986.

Sports and New Compact Model Must knowfull text

  • Only 10 sports, compared with 19 at Birmingham 2022.
  • Existing venues were reused instead of building large new stadiums; only 2715 athletes.
  • Sports included athletics, swimming, gymnastics, track cycling, netball, weightlifting, boxing, judo, bowls, 3 × 3 basketball.
  • Top three: Australia (70 gold, 171 total), England (29 gold), Canada (19 gold).
  • India 4th: 13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze = 39; Scotland 5th, also 13 gold and 39 total.

Don't confuse India and Scotland both had 13 gold and 39 medals; India was 4th, Scotland 5th.

  • Opening flag-bearer: Mirabai Chanu; baton-bearer: Lovlina Borgohain; closing flag-bearer: Jaismine Lamboria.

  • Chad le Clos (South Africa) became the most decorated Commonwealth Games athlete with his 21st medal.
